title: From Digital Accounting Capability to MSME Sustainability: The Mediating Role of Financial Reporting Quality and the Moderating Role of Financial Literacy
summary: Purpose - This study examined whether digital accounting capability was associated with the sustainability of micro, small, and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs), and whether financial reporting quality and financial literacy served as a mediator and moderator, respectively. Methodology: An explanatory cross-sectional survey of 258 MSME managers in the Special Region of Yogyakarta and Central Java, Indonesia, was analyzed using structural equation modeling with LISREL. Six hypotheses covered direct, indirect, and interaction pathways. Results: Digital accounting capability was not significantly associated with financial reporting quality or MSME sustainability. Financial reporting quality was positively associated with sustainability (coefficient = 1.45; t = 9.57). Its indirect pathway from digital accounting capability was not significant (coefficient = −0.05; t = −1.31). Financial literacy did not significantly moderate the digital accounting capability–reporting quality relationship (coefficient = 0.01; t = 1.94), but the financial reporting quality × financial literacy interaction was significant and negative (coefficient = −0.02; t = −3.84). Contribution: The results distinguish digital accounting capability from the quality of accounting information and show that financial literacy did not uniformly strengthen the tested relationships. The cross-sectional estimates support associations, not causal claims.

title: Greenwashing and Directors' Liability under the Companies Act, 2013: An Analysis of Directors' Duties in ESG Governance
summary: Greenwashing is a major concern for corporate governance as firms communicate environmental performance through sustainability reports, ESG disclosures and advertisements. It occurs when a company's environmental claims are false, misleading, exaggerated, vague or insufficiently supported by evidence. This study examines when directors can be held liable for greenwashing under the Companies Act, 2013, with reference to their statutory and fiduciary duties. The study focuses on Section 166 and also examines Sections 134, 149(12), 447 and 448, SEBI's BRSR and BRSR Core framework and the CCPA Guidelines, 2024. It is doctrinal and analytical, with a comparative study of the EU, UK, US and Australia. It finds that Indian law offers several mechanisms against greenwashing, but no comprehensive framework determines when it leads to personal director liability, and recommends stronger board-level ESG oversight, verification of sustainability information and better regulatory coordination.

title: Tingkat Pendidikan Dewan Direksi, Profitabilitas, Dan Komite Audit Terhadap Manajemen Laba
summary: This article reviews literature on the relationship between directors’ educational background, profitability, and audit committees and earnings management. The study uses a literature-review approach by examining the journal links supplied by the author and accessible publication records. The reviewed evidence indicates that the relationship between directors’ education and earnings management may depend on how knowledge and expertise are used; one study on conventional banking companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange for 2015–2019 reported a positive and significant association. Profitability findings are not uniform across measures: a study of banking companies for 2016–2017 found significant positive effects for return on assets and return on equity, while net profit margin was not significant. Evidence concerning audit committees also varies by characteristics; one manufacturing-company study for 2013–2016 found that audit committee size, financial expertise, and meeting frequency were not individually significant. Because this article does not re-estimate company-level data, the discussion is a synthesis of prior findings rather than a new statistical test. The review highlights the importance of considering the three factors jointly and acknowledging differences in samples, periods, and operational measures.

title: Factors affecting the efficiency of Vietnam's coal export supply chain
summary: This study analyzes the factors affecting the efficiency of Vietnam's coal export supply chain in the context of increasingly coordinated mining, screening, warehousing, port operations, and international trade. Based on supply chain management theory, resource-based and dynamic capability perspectives, the paper examines five groups of factors: logistics infrastructure capacity; information sharing; supply chain cooperation; logistics digitalization; and adaptability to market and institutional conditions. The research results show that the efficiency of the export supply chain is not determined by a single link but depends on the degree of synchronization between the flow of materials, information flow, and coordinated decisions between mining companies, warehousing units, ports, transportation vehicles, and export business units. Among these, logistics infrastructure capacity and supply chain cooperation play a prominent role. Information sharing, logistics digitalization, and adaptability facilitate improved delivery reliability, reduced lead times, cost control, and better responsiveness to international market fluctuations. This research contributes to the evidence-based management of bulk cargo supply chains in the mining industry, while also suggesting implications for synchronizing warehousing, port, and transportation capabilities, increasing data sharing, developing digital coordination platforms, and strengthening inter-unit coordination mechanisms within the coal export chain.

title: CONTEXT-AWARE DIGITAL TWIN ARCHITECTURES FOR REAL-TIME TRANSPORTATION AND WAREHOUSE OPTIMIZATION IN CLOUD-NATIVE SUPPLY CHAIN PLATFORMS
summary: Context-aware digital twins are emerging as enabling architectures for coordinating responses to disruptions across inventory, warehouse, and transportation operations in cloud-based supply-chain platforms. They are important because they can be used to link continually evolving operational representations with optimization services that are able to react to traffic conditions, order arrivals, equipment status, changes in inventory, and facility constraints. This article reviews peer-reviewed journal literature on digital supply-chain twins, warehouse intelligence, dynamic vehicle routing, Internet of Things-enabled logistics, microservice architectures, and computational modelling. Some studies indicate that digital-twin approaches can improve visibility, scenario evaluation, and decision coordination in specific settings, but there is very little evidence of fully integrated real-time optimization of transportation and warehouse operations. Closed-loop orchestration has not been a primary focus of existing implementations, which tend to focus on warehouse simulation or monitoring, route adjustment, or resilience analysis across logistics domains. Other limitations include insufficient semantic interoperability, inadequate model fidelity, inconsistent latency assessment, deployment evidence, and consideration of cybersecurity and human intervention. The field therefore needs architectures that integrates event-driven context management, federated twin models, scalable optimization, auditable decision services, and explicit uncertainty handling.

title: Social Sciences as a Pathway to Equitable Environmental Governance and Climate Action
summary: Global environmental challenges such as climate change, biodiversity loss, pollution, and resource depletion pose existential threats to ecosystems and human well-being. While the natural sciences provide crucial data on the scope and mechanisms of these issues, addressing them effectively requires an understanding of the human dimensions that underlie environmental degradation. Social science plays a vital role in interpreting the behavioral, cultural, political, and economic drivers of environmental change, offering tools and frameworks for creating sustainable solutions. This paper explores the interdisciplinary contributions of social science to environmental problem-solving. It highlights how disciplines such as sociology, political science, psychology, economics, and anthropology deepen our understanding of environmental behavior, policy development, governance, risk perception, and social justice. The paper also emphasizes the importance of social science in shaping equitable climate policy, enhancing public engagement, and facilitating community-based environmental action. Key frameworks such as behavioral economics, environmental justice, and socio-ecological systems thinking are examined to demonstrate how social science bridges the gap between knowledge and action. Furthermore, the paper illustrates how social science fosters interdisciplinary collaboration by integrating human and ecological systems, thus promoting resilience and long-term sustainability. As the world faces intensifying environmental crises, social science provides essential insights into how societies can adapt, transform, and respond collectively. The integration of social science into environmental discourse is not only beneficial but essential for designing inclusive, just, and effective environmental strategies.

title: Design Innovation and Collaborative Supply Chain Management in the Development of Animation Derivatives
summary: The rapid development of animation-related derivative products is undergoing a transition from full-process production in traditional factories to modularized division of tasks and supply chain collaboration. In 2025, the market size of derivative products tied to the animation industry reached RMB 652.1 billion, while the total retail value of collectible toys stood at RMB 67.69 billion, with new categories such as rotocast plush toys and AI-powered toys showing notable and sustained growth. However, beneath this rapid industry growth, the dual challenges of design homogenization on the creative side and lagging supply chain responsiveness on the manufacturing side have severely constrained both product quality and development efficiency. Drawing on comprehensive industry survey data, this paper systematically analyzes the manifestations and root causes of insufficient design innovation and supply chain collaboration failures in the development of animation derivatives. Countermeasures are proposed from four dimensions: deep intellectual property-based transformation, design process reengineering, industrial cluster collaboration, and flexible manufacturing adoption of advanced technologies. The study suggests that modular decomposition of components and specialized division of tasks provide an effective pathway to enhancing overall product quality. Furthermore, the quantitative management of supply chain collaboration plays a significant role in shortening delivery lead times and improving overall operational efficiency within the creative manufacturing sector, ultimately fostering sustainable market competitiveness.

title: Digital Transformation: a Catalyst for Institutional Efficacy in the Public Sector
summary: Public sector institutions are often characterised by service delivery delays, time management challenges, paper-based activities, and limited application of digital technologies. Digital transformation has become a crucial tool for enhancing institutional efficacy for the purposes of achieving set goals and objectives, and ultimately improved service delivery. This article explores the significance of digital transformation in enhancing institutional efficacy in public sector institutions. The Department of Home Affairs, Vhembe District served as a reference. Structured questionnaires were used to gather data from 120 officials of the Department of Home Affairs using a quantitative research method. The findings indicate that digital transformation improves service quality and speed, supports informed decision-making, enhances collaboration and communication and increases administrative efficiency and accuracy. The article highlights digital transformation as a strategic enabler of institutional performance that promotes responsive, accountable and citizen centred government. The study recommends strengthening digital infrastructure, investing in continuous staff training, integrating communication platforms and promoting citizen centred digital services.

title: Digital transformation of marketing communications in the private healthcare market
summary: The article examines the specific characteristics of the private healthcare services market and highlights the significant role of digital marketing communications in building patient relationships and enhancing patient satisfaction. To identify the key factors determining the competitiveness of private medical clinics in Yekaterinburg, the competitive environment was analyzed using Porter’s Five Forces framework. The analysis revealed a high degree of supplier bargaining power, intense intra-industry competition, and significant buyer power, represented by patients. A set of strategic measures aimed at mitigating these risks is proposed, including the development of physician brands; partnerships with medical equipment manufacturers and the implementation of proprietary digital solutions; loyalty programs and personalized health check-ups; the development of evidence-based content marketing; positioning the medical facility as a center of expert diagnostics; and personalization of patient interactions. A survey was conducted to identify patients’ preferred communication channels with medical clinics. Based on the findings, a framework for distributing content across digital platforms is proposed. The results of the study provide a basis for developing recommendations for attracting new patients and strengthening the trust of existing patients in private healthcare providers.

title: The Impact of ESG Performance on Bank Profitability: Evidence from ASEAN-5
summary: This study examines whether Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) performance contributes to bank profitability in ASEAN-5 countries. As sustainability principles increasingly shape financial markets, banks are expected not only to perform their intermediation role efficiently but also to operate ethically and responsibly. However, empirical evidence on whether ESG performance translates into tangible financial benefits remains mixed, particularly in emerging markets. Using balanced panel data of commercial banks operating in Indonesia, Malaysia, Thailand, the Philippines, and Singapore over the period 2015–2024, this study applies a Fixed Effect Model to analyze the relationship between ESG performance and bank profitability, measured by Return on Assets (ROA) and Return on Equity (ROE). The model incorporates bank-specific control variables total deposits, total loans, and total assets as well as macroeconomic conditions captured by inflation and economic growth. The empirical results show that ESG performance has a positive and statistically significant effect on both ROA and ROE, indicating that ethical banking practices enhance operational efficiency and shareholder returns. Economic growth strengthens profitability, while inflation exerts a negative effect. These findings suggest that ESG performance represents more than reputational signaling; it functions as a strategic asset that supports long-term financial performance. This study contributes to the sustainable finance literature by providing multi country empirical evidence from ASEAN-5 banks and offers insights for regulators, banks, and investors in emerging markets.

title: Transitioning to Circular Automotive Systems: A Systematic Review of Supply Chain Practices and Implementation
summary: The Automobile industry shifts from linear to circular economy for sustainability on a global level with respect to the industrial revolution 5.0, but it faces challenges when establishing circular economy.Circular supply chain implementation is dependent on multiple barriers and enablers, including economic managerial, technological, regulatory and social domains, making it ineffective for single factor solution.The purpose behind this review is to conduct a systematic literature review to develop an understanding how these interconnected barriers and enablers can together shape the circular supply chain implementation and their performance, specifically inside the automotive sector which is still remain a little known.By applying the PRISMA framework on 150 peer reviewed articles, research papers.The research shows that literature focuses on primarily on electric vehicle barriers within developing economies.Circular supply chain implementation is governed not only by isolated barriers but by complex systematic interdependencies between enablers as well.This interdependencies are of enablers and barriers can be further classified into economical and financial, managerial and organizational, technological and infrastructure, policy and regularity and market and social.The study shows two systematic patterns, driving the transition technology-policy interdependence and conflicting relationship between large scale production and value extraction.The findings also presented a research agenda focusing on strategic value creation through material streams of automotive electronics, plastics and composites with high potential value and further insights are needed.Circular supply chain as a strategic approach for securing critical material supplies, while policymakers could leverage the use of digital tools as the foundational infrastructure for subsidies allocation and prevent the fraud.

title: CAPITAL INTENSITY, GREEN INNOVATION DAN INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY SOPHISTICATION TERHADAP SUSTAINABLE BUSINESS PERFORMANCE
summary: This research investigates the effects of capital intensity, green innovation, and information technology (IT) sophistication on sustainable business performance among manufacturing companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange in 2025. The central research question addresses whether these variables have partial or simultaneous impacts on sustainable business performance. Utilizing a quantitative causal methodology, the study analyzes secondary data obtained from annual and sustainability reports. The study selected 43 manufacturing companies through purposive sampling and analyzed the data using multiple linear regression in IBM SPSS. The results indicate that green innovation has a positive and significant effect on sustainable business performance, while capital intensity and IT sophistication do not significantly influence it. These findings identify green innovation as a primary determinant of sustainable business performance. Theoretically, the study advances the literature by integrating financial and environmental performance dimensions. Practically, the results guide corporate management and policymakers in developing effective, transparent strategies to enhance sustainable business performance. title: The Impact of Supply Chain Finance Digitalization on Corporate Working Capital Management Efficiency
summary: As firms face volatile cash flows, tighter external financing, and greater pressure to coordinate financial and operating activities, supply chain finance digitalization is changing how transaction data, financing, payments, and settlement are connected. Existing studies often examine digital supply chain finance through individual financial outcomes or isolated cases, while relatively few systematically consider both its direct effects and multiple indirect transmission mechanisms on working capital management efficiency. This paper examines the effect of digital supply chain finance on corporate working capital management efficiency through a structured review and conceptual synthesis of recent literature, with a focus on direct effects and three indirect mechanisms. The evidence suggests that digital supply chain finance improves working capital efficiency by accelerating financing and settlement, reducing unnecessary capital tied up in receivables and inventories, and coordinating receivables, payables, inventories, and cash flows. Overall, the main channels are greater information transparency, better financing access, and closer financial-operational coordination. This paper constructs an analytical framework that incorporates direct effects and multiple indirect transmission mechanisms. Thereby contributing to the literature on digitalization in supply chain finance and corporate working capital management.

title: Advancing Sustainable Competitive Advantage through Green Digital Transformation Leadership, Green Technological Innovation and Green Digital Transformation: An Integrated SEM–NCA Approach
summary: ABSTRACT Environmental sustainability has raised global concerns following the increase in carbon emissions due to industrial and commercial activities. As such, this research aims to examine the association between green digital transformation leadership (GDTL) in Malaysian manufacturing companies and sustainable competitive advantage (SCA), with green digital transformation (GDT) and green technology innovation (GTI) playing mediating roles. The strategic importance of leadership in supporting green and digital development efforts is gaining ground, as reflected in Malaysia's ongoing effort to maintain a technological edge while navigating environmental issues. Survey data were gathered from 141 senior management personnel and analysed using partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS‐SEM) and necessary condition analysis (NCA). Based on the elicited outcomes, GDTL significantly increased GDT, GTI and subsequently, SCA. The GDT mediated the GDTL–SCA relationship, denoting the pathways for leadership to promote sustainability. As demonstrated by the NCA outcomes, GDT most significantly influenced SCA. Overall, this study has added depth to the current literature by (1) empirically connecting GDTL with GTI; (2) evidencing the importance of GDT to the achievement of SCA in Malaysia; and (3) providing an integrated framework linking the three components of GDTL, digital transformation, GTI and SCA. The current findings can serve as a guideline for future leaders to navigate digital and green transitions in developing nations.

title: Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning in Supply Chain Management: Applications, Evidence, Implementation Constraints, and Future Directions
summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) are increasingly investigated as decision-support technologies for supply chain management (SCM), yet their value depends on the nature of the decision, data availability, organisational capability and the methods used to evaluate outcomes. This critical narrative review examines applications across demand forecasting, inventory planning, sourcing, manufacturing, logistics, risk management and sustainability. It brings together relevant peer-reviewed reviews, conceptual contributions and empirical studies, and distinguishes evidence from operational deployments from results reported in literature syntheses or simulations. The literature supports the practical relevance of data-driven prediction, pattern detection and decision augmentation, but it does not establish uniform improvements in cost, forecast accuracy, resilience or environmental performance across settings. Reviewed research also identifies integration costs, fragmented data, process misalignment, model drift, limited transparency and governance concerns as barriers to realising benefits. Recent work on generative AI broadens possible applications to document-intensive processes, synthetic scenarios and interactive decision support, while indicating that field-based validation remains limited. A process-oriented framework is proposed in which analytics inform planning, procurement, manufacturing, distribution and inventory decisions under continuous human oversight. The review argues that useful evaluations should compare AI-supported decisions against relevant operational baselines, account for service levels and cost trade-offs, and document transferability across sectors and resource settings. Future research should prioritise longitudinal field studies, cross-organisational coordination, responsible deployment and context-sensitive applications in emerging economies.

title: Integrating Sustainability Strategy, Governance, and Outcomes: Reviewing Two‐Decades of ESG Research Through Bibliometric and Content Analysis
summary: ABSTRACT This study provides an in‐depth literature review on ESG topics. It combines bibliometric mapping of 447 publications from Scopus and WoS, along with qualitative content analysis of 249 papers. The review examines how ESG has evolved from a disclosure‐based measure into a comprehensive framework that integrates sustainable strategy, governance, and finance. The analysis identifies five main research clusters: ESG disclosure and transparency, performance measurement, ratings and evaluation, sustainable finance, and reporting frameworks. The content analysis outlines dominant theories, methods, and variable relationships, showing that ESG can act both as a driver and an outcome in empirical models. It also highlights underexplored areas such as ESG assurance, greenwashing, stakeholder influence, and contextual diversity. Future studies should strengthen conceptual and empirical connections across ESG themes, explore governance in cross‐country contexts, and evaluate the effects of mandatory disclosure regimes. Emerging technologies such as artificial intelligence, blockchain, and sustainability analytics also offer new opportunities to enhance the credibility and comparability of ESG information.

title: PERAN CSR MEMODERASI PENGARUH FINANCIAL DISTRESS DAN COMPANY GROWTH TERHADAP ERC
summary: This study aims to analyze the effect of Financial Distress (FD) and Company Growth (CG) on the Earnings Response Coefficient (ERC), as well as the moderating role of Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) disclosure in state-owned enterprises (SOEs) listed on the IDX during 2018–2023. Using a quantitative associative approach and purposive sampling, a final sample of 17 SOEs (102 panel observations) was obtained. Data were analyzed using Random Effect Model panel regression and Moderated Regression Analysis (MRA). The results show that FD (proxied by Altman Z-score) has a statistically significant positive coefficient, which economically proves that higher Financial Distress (lower Z-score) leads to a lower ERC. Conversely, CG has no significant effect on ERC due to high leverage financing asset expansion. CSR does not moderate the FD–ERC relationship (acting as a predictor moderator). However, CSR significantly moderates (quasi-moderator) the CG–ERC relationship (+2.446; p = 0.001), strengthening and transforming an insignificant asset growth signal into a positive market-appreciated signal. These findings confirm that CSR serves as a strategic tool that enhances the credibility of SOE growth in capital markets. Keywords: CSR, ERC, FG and CG.

title: The impact of digital green finance on agricultural carbon emissions: evidence from 285 Chinese cities
summary: Agriculture, a major source of greenhouse gas emissions, plays a vital role in global climate governance through its low‑carbon transition. Digital green finance (DGF) represents a promising tool for cutting agricultural carbon emissions (ACE). Based on panel data for 285 Chinese cities spanning 2011–2023, this study measures DGF via a coupling coordination model and employs a suite of econometric models, including two-way fixed effects, threshold, nonlinear mediating, and moderating effect models, to explore the causal impacts, underlying mechanisms, and heterogeneity of DGF on ACE. The main findings are as follows: (1) DGF exhibits a significant inverted U-shaped nonlinear relationship with ACE: ACE rises in the initial stage of DGF development and declines after crossing the inflection point of 0.3092. (2) The relationship is characterized by double thresholds at 0.4237 and 0.4800; DGF’s abatement effect gradually turns from statistically insignificant to strongly significant. (3) Agricultural technological innovation, agricultural industrial agglomeration and rural entrepreneurial vitality act as inverted U-shaped nonlinear mediators, whose indirect effects switch from positive to negative as DGF expands. (4) Financial regulatory intensity positively moderates this inverted‑U relationship by shifting the inflection point leftwards, flattening the curve and stabilizing long-term abatement performance. (5) DGF’s impacts on ACE exhibit pronounced multi-dimensional heterogeneity. Theoretically, this study extends research on the environmental effects of DGF to the agricultural sector and identifies its institutional prerequisites. Practically, it provides evidence-based policy implications for integrating digital and green finance into agricultural systems and shares China’s experience to support the global low-carbon transformation of agriculture.

title: Human Capital and Digitalisation in FMCG Supply Chain for Sustainable Operations: A Systematic Literature Review
summary: The Fast-Moving Consumer Goods (FMCG) business is under pressure to improve operational efficiency and solve sustainability issues in a digital world. Human capital and digitalisation drive productivity, responsiveness, and long-term competitiveness in sustainable operations. However, present research frequently isolate these elements, limiting knowledge of their combined impact. This PRISMA-guided Systematic Literature Review (SLR) examines human capital and digitisation in FMCG supply chains. Current research trends, theme insights, and knowledge gaps are reviewed. Data shows that AI, automation, predictive analytics, and the IoT boost efficiency, supply chain visibility, and decision-making. Adoption and use of these technologies require human capital, including digital skills, organisational learning, and human-machine collaboration. The analysis shows that FMCG contexts in emerging nations have underexplored human capital and digitalisation integration. The findings improve awareness of how human capital and digital capabilities support sustainable operations, and they show FMCG companies must integrate staff development with digital technology adoption. A detailed overview of their interplay and sustainable supply chain management research and practice directions are presented in this operations management paper

title: THE EFFECT OF KEY AUDIT MATTERS (KAM) DISCLOSURE, AUDIT COMMITTEE, COMPANY COMPLEXITY, AND RELATED- PARTY TRANSACTIONS ON AUDIT FEES
summary: This study aims to empirically examine and analyze the influence of Key Audit Matters (KAM) disclosure, audit committees, firm complexity, and related-party transactions on audit fees within the energy sector. The research employs a quantitative approach using panel data regression analysis. Through a purposive sampling technique, 91 energy sector companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) were identified as the population for the 2022–2024 study period. A final sample of 36 companies was selected, resulting in 108 total observations. The findings indicate that audit committees and firm complexity have a significant positive impact on audit fees for energy sector companies, whereas Key Audit Matters (KAM) and related-party transactions do not show a significant influence. These results imply that public accounting firms (KAP) consider firm complexity and the presence of an audit committee as key determinants when setting audit fees for their clients. Furthermore, the findings suggest that the implementation of KAM disclosure requirements has been successfully integrated without imposing additional costs; however, they also highlight the need for ongoing oversight regarding the risks associated with related-party transactions, which may not yet be fully reflected in the determination of audit fees within the energy sector. This research contributes to a better understanding of how Key Audit Matters, audit committees, firm complexity, and related-party transactions affect audit fees for energy sector companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange.

title: Digitalization is More Than Just a Trend: Modernizing Financial Reporting in the Halal MSME Ecosystem of the Riau Islands
summary: This study examines the modernization of financial reporting among MSMEs in Riau Islands Province, focusing on Ayuraskitchen, a home-based business in Batam City that has grown into a multi-outlet cake business. Using a descriptive qualitative approach, the study analyzes the gradual transition in financial reporting from manual records and Microsoft Excel templates to the Lamikro application and, ultimately, the digital accounting application Mekari Jurnal. The findings indicate that modernization occurred gradually in accordance with the growth and needs of the business and was supported by consistent record-keeping, government training and assistance, and the availability of accessible technology. The implementation of digital financial reporting improved the organization, efficiency, and accessibility of financial information, while supporting cash flow monitoring and faster business decision-making. Systematic financial records also help MSMEs prepare financing documentation and improve their bankability by providing more structured business information, although access to financing is influenced by other factors. The study recommends strengthening accounting and digital literacy, providing continuous assistance, implementing SAK EMKM, and fostering collaboration among MSMEs, local governments, financial institutions, and financial technology providers to accelerate the modernization of MSME financial reporting.

title: R&D Expenditure Capitalization, Choice of Earnings Management Methods, and the Tax Burden: Evidence from Chinese A-Share Listed Firms, 2016–2024
summary: The accounting choice between capitalizing and expensing R&D expenditure affects both current earnings and the current tax burden, and also serves as an important instrument of corporate earnings management. Using a sample of Chinese A-share listed firms over 2016–2024, this paper examines the effect of the R&D capitalization ratio on firms' choice of earnings management methods, and further investigates the moderating role of tax burden. We obtain four main findings. First, a higher R&D capitalization ratio is associated with a lower degree of real earnings management, whereas accrual-based earnings management exhibits no significant change once fixed effects are controlled for, indicating a substitution relationship between capitalization and real activities manipulation. Second, the decline in real earnings management arises mainly from offsetting changes in abnormal production costs and abnormal discretionary expenses; firms show no sign of overproduction or of cutting discretionary expenditures. Third, R&D capitalization significantly raises firms' effective tax rate, and this effect is concentrated in high- and new-technology enterprises, suggesting that capitalization carries an observable tax cost. Fourth, tax burden moderates the above substitution relationship, in that the inhibiting effect is stronger in the high-tax-burden group; however, the continuous interaction term is not statistically significant, so the moderating effect manifests mainly as between-group differences. Fifth, the above relationships are more pronounced in non-state-owned enterprises and in high- and new-technology enterprises. This study provides empirical evidence for understanding the economic consequences of R&D accounting choices and for improving R&D expenditure disclosure and tax incentive policies.

title: Dataset Supporting a Systematic Literature Review of Climate Change Impacts on Fisheries Trade and Supply Chains
summary: Dataset Description This dataset supports the systematic literature review entitled “Impacts of Climate Change on International Trade, Competitiveness, and Supply Chains of Fisheries Commodities: A Systematic Literature Review.” The review followed the PRISMA 2020 reporting framework and used a PECOS-informed eligibility approach. Searches conducted in Scopus, ScienceDirect, Web of Science, and PubMed identified 707 records. After removing 44 duplicates, 663 records were screened, seven full-text articles were assessed for eligibility, and six studies were included in the final synthesis. The dataset contains structured information on study selection, study-level characteristics, climate-related stressors, fisheries trade and market outcomes, supply-chain disruptions, adaptation and resilience responses, methodological quality appraisal, and outcome-level evidence extraction. The dataset is provided to support research transparency, reproducibility, and further investigation of climate change impacts on international fisheries trade and seafood supply chains. title: THE PRICE THAT IS NOT ON THE TAG: FAST FASHION, ISO 26000 AND THE BALANCING OF STAKEHOLDER INTERESTS IN INDIA Displaced Cost, Disclosed Cost and the Transmission Deficit in Indian ESG Regulation
summary: Fast fashion sells a garment at a price its production did not cost. The difference is not efficiency but displacement, the migration of production costs from the seller's income statement to parties who never contracted to bear them: the worker paid below subsistence, the watercourse receiving untreated effluent, the municipality inheriting the garment as waste, and the consumer sold an unsubstantiated sustainability claim. This paper distinguishes displaced cost from disclosed cost and argues that India's environmental, social and governance architecture, comprising the Companies Act 2013, the Business Responsibility and Sustainability Reporting framework, the four Labour Codes and the environmental consent regime, has been built almost entirely around the second. Drawing on the political economy of purchasing practices, the critical scholarship on private social auditing and the legal analysis of mandatory due diligence, it contends that the regulatory locus of the problem has migrated to the demand-side jurisdictions of the European Union, leaving India, a supply-side jurisdiction, to choose between derived compliance, arbitrage retention and autochthonous equivalence. The paper reassesses ISO 26000:2010, treating its refusal of certifiability not as institutional weakness but as a design choice matched to its object, and identifies its central defect as a transmission deficit rather than a normative one. It proposes converting section 166(2) of the Companies Act 2013 from balance-as-mention into balance-as-decision-rule, relocating due diligence from the audited factory to the placed order, and giving ISO 26000 transmission through Bureau of Indian Standards sectoral guidance, procurement conditionality and a textile extended producer responsibility scheme.

title: A Study on Integration of AI with ESG Reporting
summary: Corporates operate their businesses in a very dynamic and complex landscape. The connection between corporates, society, and the eco-system is inseparable. The way of reporting business information has changed drastically due to the changing needs of information by different stakeholders and changes in reporting frameworks. BRSR aims to standardize reporting related to ESG criteria, helping stakeholders make informed decisions regarding their investments. Traditional method of reporting often requires processing huge data from different departments, which is a time-consuming process and error prone. Integration of AI in BRSR reporting can potentially lead to numerous benefits and can mitigate the challenges of various ESG reporting frameworks. This study seeks to highlight the importance of leveraging AI in ESG Reporting with an objective to exhibit the ESG Reporting preparedness of Indian Companies and the prospects and challenges of integrating AI with ESG Reporting. title: Edible Biopolymer Coatings for Postharvest Preservation in Warm‐Chain Horticultural Supply Chain: Mechanisms, Materials, Design Strategies, and Future Directions
summary: Fresh fruit and vegetable postharvest losses reach 30%-50% between harvest and consumption, concentrated in low- and middle-income countries where warm-chain supply chains (20°C-35°C, 55%-85% relative humidity, intermittent handling) replace the refrigerated cold chains conventional technology assumes. Edible coatings from polysaccharides, proteins, and lipids offer a non-refrigeration postharvest intervention, with efficacy confirmed under controlled laboratory conditions, but commercial adoption remains marginal. This review argues that the gap between laboratory performance and field outcomes is primarily a systems-design failure, in which existing formulations optimized for stable, refrigerated conditions are not engineered to maintain function under warm-chain variability. Biopolymer materials face a three-axis trade-off, unable to simultaneously satisfy moisture barrier performance, gas exchange selectivity, and thermal-hygroscopic stability, and all three degrade predictably under warm-chain conditions through mechanisms current formulation design does not account for. Bioactive release kinetics compound this failure by depleting protection before supply chain completion, while the absence of a commodity classification framework makes the research literature noncumulative. This review makes three contributions. It provides, to the authors' knowledge, among the first integrated analyses of biopolymer coating performance failure under warm-chain conditions, distinguished by its deployment-focused approach rather than a materials-cataloging one. It formalizes this into a three-axis framework showing that composite design is physically necessary for warm-chain applications, and proposes a four-pillar warm-chain design framework comprising predictive formulation modeling, controlled-release calibration, commodity-specific coating architecture, and standardized warm-chain validation protocols. A six-phase implementation pipeline and a commodity-specific application matrix operationalize this framework into a demonstrable pathway from formulation to field deployment.

title: Research on the multidimensional impact effects of the rural digital economy on the resilience of agricultural development: evidence from 30 provinces in China
summary: This paper first explores the mechanism by which the rural digital economy (RDE) affects the resilience of agricultural development (RAD). Then, based on the data of 30 provinces in China from 2011 to 2022, the entropy method is used to measure the level of RDE and RAD. The spatial correlation of RDE and RAD is analyzed through Moran’s I and Geary’s C. Then, the direct effect of RDE on RAD, the spatial spillover effect, and the mediating effect of agricultural technological progress (ATP) were empirically tested through the bidirectional fixed effect model, the mediating effect model, and the spatial Durbin model (SDM). The research findings are as follows: (1) Both RDE and RAD in China are on the rise, and there are obvious regional differences. (2) The significant enhancement of RDE has improved RAD. This conclusion remains valid after robustness tests and endogeneity tests, and the promoting effects are more significant in the western regions, nongrain-producing areas, and regions with high policy intensity. (3) The development of RDE in local areas will have a positive spatial spillover effect on the RAD in neighboring regions. This conclusion still holds after replacing different weights, and the spillover effects are more significant in the eastern regions and major grain-producing areas. (4) ATP only has a local mediating effect in the process of RDE influencing RAD, and the spatial mediating mechanism has not yet formed. The mediating effect of ATP is more significant in the eastern region and non-major grain-producing areas.

title: Green Supply Chain Management and Economic Sustainability of Small and medium Enterprises (SMEs) in Enugu State, Nigeria
summary: The study evaluated the effect of green supply chain management on the economic sustainability of small and medium enterprises (SMEs) in Enugu State, Nigeria. The specific objectives were to determine the effect of green production on cost efficiency and assess the effect of green logistics on the revenue growth of SMEs in Enugu State, Nigeria. The study adopted a descriptive survey research design. Primary data were collected through the administration of questionnaires. The study population comprised 3,740 staff members. A sample size of 345 was determined using Freund and William’s statistical formula. Of the questionnaires distributed, 251 were returned and correctly completed. The validity of the research instrument was assessed using content analysis, and the result was satisfactory. The reliability of the instrument was tested using the Pearson correlation coefficient (r), which yielded a reliability coefficient of 0.82, indicating good reliability. Data were presented and analysed using mean scores and standard deviations based on the four-point Likert scale. The hypotheses were tested using the Z-test statistic. The findings revealed that green production had a significant positive effect on the cost efficiency of SMEs in Enugu State, Nigeria (Z = 9.673, p < .05), while green logistics had a significant positive effect on the revenue growth of SMEs in the state (Z = 9.799, p < .05). The study concluded that green supply chain management plays an important role in promoting the economic sustainability of SMEs in Enugu State, Nigeria. Among other recommendations, the study recommended that SME owners and managers in Enugu State should adopt environmentally friendly production techniques, including the use of energy-efficient equipment, waste minimisation, and the efficient use of raw materials, to reduce production costs and improve cost efficiency.

title: Algorithmic Differential Pricing in the Digital Economy: Inherent Logic and Hierarchical Industry Regulatory Framework
summary: Digital platforms implement personalized pricing relying on massive user data and algorithm technologies, and big data driven "big data ripening" has continuously triggered consumer disputes, making algorithmic differential pricing a key challenge for digital economy governance. Taking algorithmic differential pricing as the research object, this paper draws on theories of price discrimination, behavioral pricing and regulatory economics and adopts theoretical analysis and logical deduction to explore its operational logic. Algorithmic differential pricing represents traditional price discrimination adapted to digital contexts. Supported by user data portraits, it realizes personalized "thousands of people, thousands of prices" and approximates first degree price discrimination. The outcome of algorithmic tiered pricing hinges on data advantages, user lock in and market competition, and its welfare effect is dual sided rather than simply beneficial or detrimental to markets. This paper establishes a hierarchical industry differentiated regulatory framework covering flexible supervision, stringent supervision and bottom line protection to reconcile industrial market features and consumer rights demands. It extends theoretical studies on algorithmic price discrimination and offers references for prudent regulatory practice for platform algorithmic pricing.

title: Tax planning, ESG disclosure, and firm value: Does ESG act as a reputational buffer? Evidence from consumer goods firms
summary: This study examines the effect of tax planning on firm value, viewed as the market's assessment of reputational capital, and the moderating role of Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) disclosure. Two competing predictions are tested: ESG disclosure acts as a reputational buffer that mitigates market penalties for tax planning, or it amplifies those penalties by signalling inconsistency. The sample comprises 10 branded consumer goods manufacturers listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange over 2022–2024 (30 firm-year observations). Tax planning is measured by the Cash Effective Tax Rate (CETR), ESG disclosure by a GRI Standards-based disclosure index, and firm value by the natural logarithm of Tobin's Q. Moderated regression with mean-centred variables and firm-clustered standard errors is employed. The results show that CETR is positively associated with firm value, implying that firms with more intensive tax planning tend to be valued lower; however, this association is significant only at the 10% level and is not robust to firm fixed effects. ESG disclosure has no direct effect and does not moderate the relationship, so neither the buffer nor the amplifier hypothesis is supported. The findings suggest that the market does not yet use the breadth of ESG disclosure to assess corporate tax behaviour, underscoring the need for explicit tax transparency.

title: ESG‐linked Executive Compensation and Firm Value: The Mediating Role of Environmental Innovation and Moderating Role of ESG Training
summary: ABSTRACT This study examines whether environmental, social, and governance (ESG)‐linked executive compensation influences firm value and the channels through which its effects emerge. Using panel data of listed firms from STOXX Europe 600 during 2015–2023, the study employs Tobin's Q and price‐to‐book value to assess firm value and robustness, respectively. The empirical analysis uses firm‐ and year‐fixed–effects models complemented by system‐generalized method of moments (GMM) and an event‐study difference‐in‐differences design to address endogeneity. The results show that ESG‐linked compensation is positively associated with environmental innovation. In the baseline fixed‐effects estimates, moving from no ESG‐linked pay to ESG‐linked pay is associated with a 7.6‐point increase in the environmental innovation score, equivalent to approximately 14% of its sample mean, and approximately 5.2% higher firm value. However, the association with firm value is not robust under system‐GMM and event‐study specifications. ESG‐related training conditions the ESG‐linked pay–environmental innovation relation; governance variables do not show consistent moderating effects. The mediation analysis does not support a statistically significant indirect effect. Overall, ESG‐linked pay appears to influence firm behavior more consistently compared with immediate financial outcomes.

title: Tourism, Hospitality and Digital Transformation in India: Economic Contributions, Employment, and Pathways to Sustainable Growth
summary: Tourism and hospitality contribute significantly to India's economic development through employment, foreign exchange earnings, investment, entrepreneurship, and demand in other industries. Other factors also influence the sector's contribution to development. Digital transformation, enabled by online travel agencies, mobile money, artificial intelligence (AI), analytics, CRM, and smart destination technologies, offers opportunities to reduce transaction costs, expand market reach, improve productivity, and enhance visitor experiences. However, challenges such as limited digital skills among small businesses, platform dependence, cyber threats, privacy concerns, algorithmic biases, and job losses must be addressed. This paper analyzes the tourism and hospitality sector's impact on the Indian economy and how technology affects the sector's growth and development. Using a qualitative, exploratory approach with secondary data from government publications, policies, and academic literature, the paper discusses the significance of productivity, employment, inclusiveness, technology, and resilience.

title: Resilience assessment and prediction of fresh agricultural product supply chains using variable fuzzy recognition and machine learning
summary: Fresh agricultural products are highly perishable and sensitive to transportation, storage, and handling conditions, which makes their supply chains particularly vulnerable to disruptions. Such disruptions can interrupt product flows and reduce both quality and availability. Traditional risk analysis methods mainly focus on uncertainty and the probability of adverse events, but they do not adequately capture the ability of supply chains to recover and adapt following disruptions. To address this limitation, this study develops a resilience evaluation and prediction framework for fresh agricultural product supply chains (FAPSCs). The framework is structured around three dimensions: production, transportation, and consumption. A hybrid modeling approach is proposed by integrating variable fuzzy set theory with machine learning. The variable fuzzy set model is used for dynamic resilience assessment, while a convolutional neural network (CNN) is employed to capture temporal dynamics and perform prediction. Indicator weights are determined by combining the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) and the CRITIC method to improve robustness and interpretability. Using panel data from 31 provinces in China from 2009 to 2023, the results show that the proposed framework effectively distinguishes different resilience levels across regions. The CNN model captures temporal variations, including peak and off-peak fluctuations, and outperforms baseline models such as Decision Tree, Random Forest, and Linear Regression, particularly in modeling nonlinear patterns and high-resilience cases. Overall, the proposed approach demonstrates strong robustness under limited or noisy data conditions and provides practical support for early warning, risk mitigation, and decision making in FAPSC management.

title: Digital Transformation and Labour Productivity in SADC: Long-Run Effects and The Limits of Human-Capital Complementarity
summary: This study examines whether digital transformation is associated with higher labour productivity in the Southern African Development Community (SADC) and whether the relationship strengthens with human capital. A fully open panel is constructed from World Development Indicators and Penn World Table 11.0 for 13 SADC economies over 2005-2023. Digitalisation is measured by the first principal component of internet use, mobile subscriptions and fixed broadband. The empirical strategy combines country fixed effects with Driscoll-Kraay covariance and a pooled dynamic common correlated effects error-correction model. Country-cluster bootstrap inference, an equal-weight digital index, sequential country deletion and threshold estimation provide robustness checks. The long-run digital coefficient is positive (0.239; 95% bootstrap interval [0.033, 0.425]), while the error-correction coefficient indicates stable annual adjustment (-0.566; interval [-0.820, -0.208]). The digitalisation-human-capital interaction is not supported (-0.041; interval [-0.102, 0.015]), and the threshold slope difference also includes zero. H2 is rejected for the aggregate PWT human-capital index, not for skills in general. The findings identify a durable average digital productivity premium without evidence that national education stocks automatically magnify it. Policy should combine reliable connectivity with targeted, use-specific capabilities and business-ecosystem coordination.

title: Assessing the impact of digital transformation on healthcare performance: A case study of healthcare establishments in the province of Midelt
summary: In Morocco, digitalization now stands among the primary levers for modernizing the healthcare sector, and a national programme supports the digital overhaul of care delivery and of the establishments providing it. Whether such change translates into better performance remains an open empirical question. The present study puts that question to the test in the province of Midelt, a mountainous territory characterised by a dispersed population and by highly uneven access to services. A structured questionnaire was administered to 103 healthcare professionals who mobilise digital tools in their daily work, and perceived performance was measured through four dimensions drawn from the literature, namely efficiency, quality of care, accessibility and equity of services. Descriptive statistics, Pearson correlations and multiple linear regression were computed with IBM SPSS Statistics (v.26). The model explains 60.4% of the variance in perceived performance. Two predictors reach significance, service efficiency (β = 0.371, p < 0.001) and quality of care (β = 0.342, p < 0.001), which supports H1 and H2. Accessibility (p = 0.273) and equity (p = 0.127) remain below the significance threshold, an outcome traced to local constraints, starting with a telemedicine programme still confined to the pilot stage. The findings plead for patient-centred digital solutions, sustained investment in suitable tools and continuous strengthening of the digital skills of healthcare personnel.

title: INVENTORY MATERIALITY DETERMINATION AND AUDITOR’S OPINION
summary: Our study explores the significance of materiality levels in inventory audits and their influence on independent auditors’ opinions, a crucial aspect of financial reporting and decision-making. Specifically, our study investigates how factors such as gender, age, education level, audit experience, and the number of files audited influence materiality assessment, audit planning, participation in audit techniques, and ultimately, auditors’ opinions on inventory audits. We employ an online survey methodology, targeting auditors from firms authorized by the Public Oversight Authority in Istanbul. Our findings reveal notable variations in audit practices, particularly regarding materiality levels, audit approaches, planning strategies, and inventory auditing techniques. Furthermore, incorrect materiality assessments appear to contribute to inaccurate audit opinions, underlining the importance of precise evaluation methods. Finally, the techniques applied in inventory auditing play a crucial role in shaping auditors’ final conclusions.

title: Evaluating Efficiency Differences in Supply Chain Practices: Evidence from Indian SMEs Using the Mann–Whitney U Test
summary: Small and medium enterprises (SMEs) supply the majority of India's manufacturing employment, yet the efficiency consequences of how they organise their supply chains remain thinly documented relative to large-firm evidence.This study compares supply chain efficiency between SMEs operating integrated supply chain practices and those operating traditional, fragmented practices, using a cross-sectional survey of 400 registered Indian SMEs and the Mann-Whitney U test.Efficiency is measured across six domains procurement and sourcing, inventory management, logistics and distribution, information integration, supplier relationships, and demand planning plus a composite index.Because the response distributions are ordinal, non-normal in every domain, and heteroscedastic across arms, a rank-based test is the appropriate inferential instrument; the analysis reports tie-corrected z statistics, Cliff's δ with bootstrap confidence intervals, and Hodges-Lehmann shift estimates rather than p-values alone.Integrated-practice firms rank significantly higher on the composite index (U = 24,416.0,z = 5.90, p < .001,δ = 0.360) and on five of the six domains after Holm correction.The advantage is largest for information integration (δ = 0.416) and demand planning (δ = 0.307), and statistically indistinguishable from zero for supplier relationships (δ = 0.063, p = .299).The composite result survives rank analysis of covariance on firm size, enterprise resource planning presence, export orientation and age, and an exactly matched 113-pair subsample.The pattern suggests that practice integration in Indian SMEs delivers its returns through informational and planning coordination rather than through relational quality, which appears to be achieved by traditional firms through other means.Implications for SME managers, cluster development agencies and non-parametric practice in operations research are discussed.

title: Pengaruh Green Management, Digital Transformation, Dan Innovation Capability Terhadap Msmes Performance (Studi Kasus Pada Kuliner Di Bogor)
summary: Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) in the culinary sector in Bogor City and Regency play a strategic role in the regional economy, yet still face challenges in enhancing competitiveness and sustainable performance amid the demands of digitalization and environmental sustainability. This study aims to analyze the influence of Green Management (GM), Digital Transformation Management (DTM), and Innovation Capability (IC) on MSMEs Performance (MP). This quantitative research employs an explanatory research design, collecting data through questionnaires distributed to 200 culinary MSME actors in Bogor City and Regency, selected using purposive sampling. The data were analyzed using SPSS, grounded in the Resource-Based View and Dynamic Capabilities Theory. The results show that GM, DTM, and IC have a positive influence on MP. These findings indicate that strengthening green practices, digital transformation, and innovation capability collectively contribute to improving the performance of culinary MSMEs. This confirms that the improvement of culinary MSME performance can be driven through the integrated optimization of these three factors

title: Machine Learning Utilisation and Perceived Financial Reporting Quality among Employees of Selected Listed Deposit Money Banks in Nigeria: A PLS-SEM Analysis
summary: Machine learning (ML) is increasingly used in accounting and assurance processes, yet focused evidence on its relationship with financial reporting quality (FRQ) in Nigerian banking remains limited. This study examines the association between ML utilisation and perceived FRQ among employees of selected listed Deposit Money Banks (DMBs) in Nigeria. A quantitative cross-sectional survey design was used. The study population comprised 243 eligible employees; 181 questionnaires were distributed after allowing for anticipated non-response, 151 completed questionnaires were returned, and all 151 were valid for analysis, yielding a response rate of 83.43%. ML and perceived FRQ were measured with five indicators each on a five-point Likert scale. PLS-SEM was implemented in SmartPLS 4. The measurement model demonstrated strong indicator loadings, reliability, and convergent validity, although the very high reliability coefficients warrant assessment of possible item redundancy. ML utilisation was positively associated with perceived FRQ (β = 0.719, t = 12.63, p < 0.001, 95% CI [0.631, 0.788]). The model explained 51.7% of the variance in perceived FRQ (R² = 0.517; adjusted R² = 0.514), with a large effect size (f² = 1.07). Because the design is cross-sectional and perception-based, the findings are interpreted as associations rather than causal effects. The study contributes focused evidence on ML utilisation and perceived financial-reporting quality in the Nigerian listed-banking context.

title: Analysis of PT Allo Bank Indonesia’s Financial Soundness Using the RGEC Method: A Case Study of 2019–2024
summary: The digital transformation of banking has increased the importance of assessing bank soundness, particularly among digital banks. This study evaluates PT Allo Bank Indonesia Tbk during 2019–2024 using the Risk Profile, Good Corporate Governance (GCG), Earnings, and Capital (RGEC) framework. A descriptive quantitative approach was applied using secondary data from annual reports. Six indicators were examined: Non-Performing Loan (NPL), Loan to Deposit Ratio (LDR), GCG rating, Return on Assets (ROA), Net Interest Margin (NIM), and Capital Adequacy Ratio (CAR). NPL declined from 10.16% in 2019 to below 1% during 2021–2024, while LDR peaked at 163.19% in 2022. GCG improved from a rating of 3 to 2, and ROA and CAR strengthened. The composite score rose from 66.67% in 2019 to 86.67% in 2021, then stabilized at 83.33% during 2022–2024. The average was 80.00%, indicating improved bank soundness, although liquidity risk remained a concern.

summary: This document provides the complete intellectual property specification, problem analysis, architectural framework, and mitigation strategies for "PoFi" (Pocket Finance)—an automated behavioral fintech ecosystem tailored for Malaysian university students and youths. title: Training Quality and Management Support as Predictors of Employee Adaptability to Digital Transformation: A Multivariate Analysis of Commercial Banks in South-East Nigeria
summary: Nigerian commercial banks have invested heavily in digital infrastructure over the last decade, yet workforce preparedness for the systems that infrastructure supports remains uneven, and the sociological literature on reskilling in developing-economy banking contexts is thin. This study examined whether two features of reskilling provision, training quality and management support, predict two dimensions of employee adaptability to digital transformation, namely willingness to adopt new digital technologies and job performance in digital banking tasks. Data were drawn from 542 employees across eight commercial banks operating in Abia, Anambra, and Imo States. A cross-sectional survey design was used, and four directional hypotheses were tested through multivariate multiple regression, with age, years of service, and job role entered as covariates. All four hypotheses were supported at p <.001. Training quality explained approximately 16.2 per cent of the multivariate variance in adoption willingness and 17.6 per cent in digital job performance, the largest effect in the study. Management support explained 14.7 per cent of the variance in adoption willingness and 15.8 per cent in digital job performance. Digital transformation maturity and technological intensity of the bank produced smaller but statistically detectable moderating effects. Interpreted through Human Capital Theory, Dynamic Capabilities Theory, and Castells’ Network Society Theory, the findings suggest that adaptability outcomes in South-East Nigerian banking depend more on the actual quality of reskilling and on the character of managerial support than on training volume or on the digital sophistication of the institution. Implications for bank human resource practice, sector regulation, and future research are set out.

title: From Decentralized to Centralized Shariah Governance: A Proposal for a Central Shariah Supervisory Board in Türkiye
summary: Shariah governance plays a critical role in ensuring that financial institutions operate in accordance with Islamic principles, mitigating the risk of Shariah non-compliance, and strengthening confidence in the broader Islamic finance sector. Currently, the regulatory framework in Türkiye exhibits several structural shortcomings, including the absence of a central and binding authority covering the entire sector, limited institutional scope, weak legal enforceability, insufficient transparency, and the lack of independent external audit mechanisms. Existing literature highlights significant gaps in the design of a comprehensive central advisory board model, particularly within the Turkish context. Addressing this critical gap, the present study proposes the establishment of an Asian-style Central Shariah Advisory Board (CSAB) specifically tailored to Türkiye. In this study, Türkiye's existing Shariah governance structure was comprehensively analyzed using comparative qualitative research methods, drawing insights from international standards (such as AAOIFI and IFSB) and the two-tier Malaysian governance model. The proposed centralized structure aims to ensure that all rulings and standards are strictly binding across diverse sectors—including participation banks, takaful, and fintech—while maintaining consistency with international best practices and building upon Türkiye's accumulated local experience. By filling these institutional and legal gaps in Shariah governance, the proposed CSAB model seeks to significantly enhance investor trust in Islamic financial institutions and sustainably strengthen Türkiye's strategic aspiration to become a leading global hub for Islamic finance.

title: The Impact of Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) Disclosure and Mining Commodity Price Volatility on Stock Returns for Mining Sector Companies on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (2019–2023)
summary: This study examines the impact of Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) Disclosure and commodity price volatility on the stock returns of mining companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) during the 2019–2023 period. Based on signaling theory, In resource-intensive industries, ESG disclosure serves as a non-financial signal that lessens information asymmetry and directs investment choices. Indonesian mining companies face pressure from regulators and investors for comprehensive sustainability reporting, yet much of the disclosure remains symbolic amid fluctuations in global commodity markets such as coal, gold, and nickel. Previous studies have shown mixed results regarding the impact of ESG, while commodity volatility adds external uncertainty to stock performance. This study addresses these gaps by investigating: (1) whether ESG disclosures significantly affect stock returns, and (2) the role of commodity price volatility in this relationship. Using a quantitative method via multiple linear regression on 26 companies (130 firm-year observations), ESG is measured using Refinitiv scores and volatility using monthly price standard deviations. These findings aim to provide insights for investors and managers regarding sustainability signals in emerging markets.

title: Exploring the Emergence and Strategic Evolution of an Emerging Fintech MicroBank in Zimbabwe Operating in a VUCA Environment
summary: This paper examines the emergence and strategic evolution of InnBucks MicroBank Limited, a Zimbabwean Microfinance organisation that evolved from a restaurant-change management digital wallet into a licensed deposit-taking microfinance bank serving around 3 million users within 4 years. Operating in what is arguably one of the most extreme VUCA (volatile, uncertain, complex, ambiguous) environments globally, characterised by currency failures, chronic hyperinflation, regulatory unpredictability, and severe infrastructure deficits, InnBucks offers a compelling case for exploring how organisations emerge, adapt, and scale amid genuine chaos. The analysis incorporates five theoretical frameworks: Chaos Theory, Entrepreneurial Orientation Theory, Disruptive Innovation and Frugal Innovation, the Viable System Model, and Strategic Decision-Making Theory. These are utilised to explain InnBucks' institutional pivots, its evolution to a registered deposit taking microfinance, its utilisation of Simbisa Brands' restaurant network as financial infrastructure, and its recent shift to cloud-native banking through the Mambu/AWS partnership. The paper proposes the ARISE (Agility, Resilience, Innovation, Systemic, Entrepreneurial) conceptual framework, which combines five theoretical perspectives into a practical model to steer strategic emergence in resource-limited, institutionally fragile environments. It concludes that InnBucks' trajectory challenges traditional assumptions about the prerequisites for financial innovation and provides transferable insights for emerging organisations operating within Sub-Saharan Africa's growing fintech ecosystem.

title: THE STRATEGIC ROLE OF GCG IN MODERATING THE EFFECT OF IOS AND ENVIRONMENTAL PERFORMANCE ON FIRM VALUE
summary: The purpose of this study is to investigate the impact of the investment opportunity set (IOS) and environmental performance on firm value, with good corporate governance (GCG) serving as a moderating variable. The method used in this study is quantitative, utilizing secondary data obtained from annual reports and sustainability reports of manufacturing companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange for the period 2021–2025. Purposive sampling was applied to determine the sample, resulting in 60 companies. For data analysis, panel data regression and Moderated Regression Analysis (MRA) were used. The findings of this study indicate that the IOS and environmental performance have a significant positive influence on firm value. Additionally, GCG enhances the influence of environmental performance on firm value but does not act as a moderator for the impact of the IOS on firm value. These results indicate that investors not only consider a company’s growth potential but also pay attention to environmental responsibility and good governance standards when assessing corporate value. This study contributes to the development of signaling theory and stakeholder theory by reinforcing the aspects of corporate governance and sustainability. The limitations of this study include a sample focused solely on the manufacturing sector and a short observation period. Future research is recommended to expand the sample to other industrial sectors, extend the observation period, and explore alternative moderating variables. title: Employing Content Analysis in ESG Research: A Systematic Review and Future Research Agenda
summary: ABSTRACT This study systematically reviews the application of content analysis in environmental, social and governance (ESG) disclosure research. Although content analysis is widely employed to examine ESG reporting, methodological approaches, disclosure channels and analytical practices remain fragmented, limiting methodological coherence and the cumulative development of knowledge. To synthesise this evolving field, 170 peer‐reviewed articles published in ABS 3, 4 and 4* journals were systematically reviewed following the PRISMA guidelines. Using bibliometric and thematic analyses, the study examines publication trends, methodological developments, disclosure channels and emerging research directions. The findings reveal substantial growth in ESG content analysis research alongside increasing methodological diversification, while also identifying important gaps relating to computational methods, disclosure channels and methodological standardisation. Building on these findings, the study develops an integrative framework grounded in the Ontology–Epistemology–Methodology (OEM) perspective to explain how methodological choices shape the interpretation of ESG disclosures. In addition, a Theory–Context–Characteristics–Methodology (TCCM)–based future research agenda comprising eight research propositions is proposed to guide future scholarship. By providing a conceptually integrated synthesis of methodological developments and future research priorities, this review advances understanding of ESG content analysis and offers practical guidance for researchers investigating corporate sustainability communication.

title: Leveraging Digital Transformation Tools to Enhance Conceptual Understanding in Secondary School Mathematics: A Systematic Review of Pedagogy, Equity and Human Capital Development
summary: Digital transformation tools are increasingly promoted as strategic resources for improving mathematics learning, yet their contribution to conceptual understanding remains uneven across school systems. This systematic literature review examines how dynamic mathematics software, virtual manipulatives, adaptive learning systems, educational games and collaborative digital environments enhance conceptual understanding in secondary school mathematics. Guided by constructivist learning theory, cognitive load theory, socio-cultural theory and technological pedagogical content knowledge, the review synthesises peer-reviewed literature published between 2015 and 2025, supported by PRISMA-informed searching, screening and thematic analysis. The final synthesis shows that digital tools support conceptual understanding when they enable multiple representations, dynamic visualisation, feedback-rich exploration, personalised pathways and mathematical discourse. However, these benefits are conditional rather than automatic. Teacher digital-pedagogical competence, assessment alignment, cognitive design quality, learner language, infrastructure and equitable access mediate whether digital transformation becomes meaningful learning or merely tool substitution. The review contributes to business and social science scholarship by positioning the digital transformation of mathematics as an educational, social equity, and human capital development issue. It argues that secondary mathematics systems require coherent investment in teacher capability, curriculum redesign, responsible data use and inclusive infrastructure. The paper concludes that digital transformation should be governed as a pedagogical and systemic reform process, not as a technological intervention alone.

title: The Gulf Cooperation Council as an Emerging Global Digital Corridor: Geo-Economic and Geopolitical Recalibration through Tech Connectivity
summary: The GCC countries have accelerated their shift from energy-centric to digital economies through significant investments in digital infrastructure, fintech and regulatory frameworks. This regional recalibration will have long-standing global implications, particularly as countries push towards increased digital connectivity, wherein, the location of the GCC states would serve as a vital lynchpin in linking Europe to South and East Asia. The article examines the GCC’s growing role in techological governance, data infrastructure and analysis, arguing that this digital turn should be viewed as a step towards economic diversification and geo-economic and geopolitical reconfiguration through data connectivity, data management, and technological innovation.Using the geo-economic framework, the article embeds the emerging GCC digital corridor within the IMEC , and highlights the digital connectivity aspect. From the techno-geopolitical perspective, the intermediary positioning of the GCC in East-West connectivity provides it a nuanced hedging strategy to select partners and reinforce its strategic autonomy .
