title: Forensic Accounting Literacy and Accounting Students’ Perceptions of Fraud Prevention in Makassar City: A Literature Review
summary: Fraud is an important issue for accounting education because students are expected not only to understand financial recording and reporting, but also to recognize irregularities, evaluate evidence, and uphold professional integrity. This article examines the relationship between forensic accounting literacy, accounting students' perceptions, and fraud prevention, while positioning Makassar City as the setting for the educational implications of the review. A literature review method is employed through narrative-thematic synthesis of empirical studies that address forensic accounting knowledge and skills, fraud awareness, fraud literacy, fraud detection capability, and fraud prevention strategies. The synthesis indicates that knowledge, analytical ability, professional skepticism, anti-fraud awareness, and investigative techniques tend to strengthen individuals' readiness to identify fraud risks and support preventive action. Evidence also shows that knowledge does not always translate directly into anti-fraud behavior because its effect may depend on motivation, professional skepticism, ethical conditions, and control systems. For accounting students in Makassar City, the findings highlight the value of forensic accounting education that combines conceptual understanding with case analysis, red-flag identification, investigative exercises, ethics, and communication of findings. The review offers a conceptual basis for universities to strengthen anti-fraud education and provides a foundation for future survey research that measures students' perceptions directly

title: PENGARUH AUDIT CAPACITY STRESS, TIME PRESSURE, DAN DUE PROFESSIONAL CARE TERHADAP KUALITAS AUDIT PADA AUDITOR DI KANTOR AKUNTAN PUBLIK KOTA MEDAN
summary: Abstract: This study aims to analyze the effect of Audit Capacity Stress, Time Pressure, and Due Professional Care on audit quality among auditors at Public Accounting Firms (KAP) in Medan, both partially and simultaneously. This study employed a quantitative approach using primary data collected through questionnaires distributed to 60 auditors working at KAPs in Medan. The sample was selected using purposive sampling. Data were analyzed using multiple linear regression with the assistance of SPSS version 26, while hypothesis testing was conducted using the t-test and F-test at a 5% significance level. The results indicate that Audit Capacity Stress has a positive and significant effect on audit quality, with a t-value of 3.141 and a significance value of 0.003. Time Pressure also has a positive and significant effect, with a t-value of 3.602 and a significance value of 0.001. Due Professional Care has a positive and significant effect, with a t-value of 3.881 and a significance value of 0.000. Simultaneously, the three independent variables significantly affect audit quality, with an F-value of 120.735 and a significance value of 0.000. The R² value of 0.866 indicates that 86.6% of the variation in audit quality is explained by the three variables. Thus, audit quality is associated with work pressure conditions and the application of professional care and diligence by auditors. Keyword: audit capacity stress; time pressure; due professional care; audit quality. Penelitian ini menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif dengan data primer yang diperoleh melalui penyebaran kuesioner kepada KAP Kota Medan, sehingga diperoleh 7 KAP dengan 60 auditor yang menjadi sampel. title: STRATEGIC HUMAN RESOURCE MANAGEMENT, DIGITAL COMMERCE, AND AI-DRIVEN MARKETING: AN INTEGRATED FRAMEWORK FOR SUSTAINABLE BUSINESS GROWTH AND ORGANIZATIONAL PERFORMANCE
summary: Digital transformation has intensified the need for organizations to align workforce strategy, digital commerce systems, and intelligent marketing capabilities. This comprehensive review examines how strategic human resource management, digital commerce, and AI-driven marketing support sustainable business growth and organizational performance. The review synthesizes literature on digital workforce planning, reskilling, platform-based commerce, marketing automation, predictive analytics, customer personalization, employee engagement, organizational resilience, and ethical governance. The findings indicate that strategic human resource management provides the capability foundation by developing digital skills, adaptive leadership, cross-functional collaboration, and continuous learning. Digital commerce serves as the value-creation and delivery infrastructure through online platforms, fintech integration, omnichannel systems, and network-based business models. AI-driven marketing serves as the customer-intelligence mechanism by enabling segmentation, forecasting, automation, personalization, and real-time engagement. Their coordinated integration can strengthen innovation, productivity, customer experience, revenue generation, and resilience. However, sustainable outcomes depend on reliable data, employee trust, human oversight, privacy protection, algorithmic fairness, and accountable governance. The review proposes an integrated framework linking people, commerce, and marketing capabilities through innovation, efficiency, engagement, and customer value. Future research should empirically test this framework across industries, firm sizes, and national contexts using longitudinal and standardized performance measures. It identifies research priorities concerning human–AI collaboration, digital inclusion, and environmental performance measurement.

title: Entrepreneurial Orientation and Strategic Agility in VUCA Africa: Developing an Ambidextrous Strategic Emergence Model for FinTech organisations
summary: This conceptual theory-building study examines how African FinTech organisations navigate volatility, uncertainty, complexity and ambiguity (VUCA), using Mukuru as a paradigmatic single case. It develops the Mukuru Ambidextrous Strategic Emergence Model (MASEM) by integrating Entrepreneurial Orientation, Strategic Agility, Organisational Ambidexterity, Chaos Theory and Strategic Decision-Making Theory. Using secondary evidence, longitudinal organisational analysis and abductive cross-theoretical synthesis, the study explains how Mukuru combines exploitation of established remittance and agent-network capabilities with exploration of digital innovation. The analysis identifies multidexterity, the orchestration of multiple, potentially contradictory business models across heterogeneous regulatory settings, as a key capability linking strategic agility to sustained emergence. MASEM conceptualises VUCA pressures as external conditions, entrepreneurial and adaptive capabilities as the strategic core, responsible AI and green digital finance as enabling capabilities, and resilience, inclusion and antifragility as intended organisational outcomes. The model is conceptual rather than empirically validated; accordingly, future research should test its constructs and causal relationships across multiple African FinTech organisations. The study contributes an Africa-centred framework and practical guidance for managers seeking to align innovation, governance, sustainability and regulatory adaptability under persistent environmental turbulence.

title: Impact of Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) Practices on Corporate Financial Performance in the Mining Sector of Zimbabwe
summary: This study examines the impact of environmental, social and governance (ESG) practices on corporate financial performance in Zimbabwe's mining sector using a case study of Zimplats Holdings Limited. The main aim was to determine whether and to what extent ESG practices contribute to financial outcomes at the firm level. The objective of the study was to examine the overall ESG and financial performance relationship, to analyse the effects of individual ESG dimensions on financial performance, and to assess the moderating role of firm-specific factors on ESG practices. Informed by the stakeholder theory, the resource-based view, and legitimacy theory, a quantitative approach was adopted, using secondary data extracted from Zimplats' Integrated Annual Reports (2023–2025) through a structured data extraction template aligned with GRI standards. Key findings reveal a positive but lagged ESG and financial performance relationship. Governance emerged as the most stable and financially material ESG pillar, while environmental and social investments showed transitional efficiency deterioration before expected long-term gains. Firm-specific factors such as asset expansion, capital structure, production volume, and multinational ownership, significantly moderated the timing and magnitude of financial returns, compressing short-term profitability indicators such as return on assets (ROA) and return on equity (ROE). The study contributes firm-level empirical evidence on unlisted Zimbabwean mining firms, extending ESG theory to emerging market contexts. Recommendations include targeting governance enhancements for immediate financial returns, allowing longer investment horizons for environmental and social initiatives, and maintaining conservative capital structures to sustain ESG investment during earnings volatility.

title: THE ROLE OF DIGITALIZATION IN IMPROVING THE EFFECTIVENESS OF INTERNAL CONTROL IN GOVERNMENT INSTITUTIONS: A LITERATURE REVIEW
summary: Advances in information technology have driven a digital transformation in financial management and government governance. This study aims to analyze the role of digitalization in enhancing the effectiveness of internal controls within government agencies, utilizing a literature review approach. The analysis examines various scholarly articles and academic documents published between 2015 and 2025. The findings indicate that the implementation of integrated information systems—such as e-government, e-budgeting, Financial Management Information Systems (FMIS), the Agency-Level Financial Application System (SAKTI), and Regional Government Information Systems (SIPD)—improves transparency, accountability, the quality of financial reporting, and the effectiveness of monitoring, while also supporting more informed decision-making. Furthermore, digitalization contributes to mitigating the risk of fraud through data integration and process automation. However, its success is contingent upon human resource competence, information technology governance, cybersecurity, and the organization's internal control culture.

title: Mapping Strategic Themes and Clusters in Lean-Green Operations Management Strategies and Sustainability Performance: A Bibliometric Analysis
summary: This study aims to map the strategic themes and research clusters related to lean-green operations management strategies and sustainability performance. A bibliometric analysis was conducted using a structured workflow supported by Biblioshiny, the web-based interface of the Bibliometrix R package. The dataset comprised 798 peer-reviewed articles published between 2019 and 2025, retrieved from scientific databases, including Web of Science, Scopus, and MDPI. Performance analysis and science mapping were conducted using Bibliometrix and Biblioshiny. The findings identified five well-established motor themes: sustainable performance, lean manufacturing, green supply chain management, green innovation, and the circular economy, which represent the core areas of the research field. Three niche themes, including green human resource management and environmental frameworks, reflect specialized research areas, while emerging themes such as lean production and lean thinking indicate evolving research frontiers. Four basic themes, including dynamic capabilities and sustainability performance measurement, highlight critical gaps in theoretical and empirical development. The study proposes a conceptual framework linking lean-green operations management strategies with sustainability performance, providing firms with a pathway to achieve operational excellence while advancing environmental and social sustainability. This study contributes to the literature by integrating lean and green operations management perspectives and offering a knowledge roadmap that connects foundational concepts with emerging themes and future research directions.

title: The Guardrail Was Right: Auditing a Token-Compression Gateway Against a Standard Benchmark
summary: We built a complete prompt-compression gateway – interval-level protection guardrails, damage-typed fidelity checks, a fail-open reverse proxy, and a three-state circuit breaker – and then audited it under the official LongBench protocol (6 QA datasets x 60 samples, official metrics, prompts, and generation limits; 1,800 real LLM calls). The audit voided our own headline numbers. The production ``safe'' mode saves 0.5\ the aggressive mode saves 63.5\ matching the classical BM25 baseline (0.968 at 49.2\ beating it. The guardrails, which had capped synthetic-benchmark savings at levels far below our earlier claims, were right: LongBench contexts are 207 topically homogeneous Wikipedia candidates, exactly the regime where unit-level relevance filtering has nothing to remove. The value of the system survives, but it migrates to three places we did not expect: (1) reliability – under 5/5 injected faults the fail-open proxy delivered every request upstream, and the circuit breaker saved 54 s of dead waiting under a killed service while never falling back on 429; (2) cache-aware economics – with provider-side prefix caching billed at 1/20 of the miss price, compressing the stable prefix destroys cache-aligned savings (a 48\ yielded only 14.1\ retrieval tail converts 23.1\ and (3) reader dependence – the same model gains $+35.7\ accuracy from compression under a truncated 4k context and loses $14.5\ reader-scaling findings. We distill these into an offline planner criterion – compression value = uncached-token share x reader noise sensitivity – which recommends ``do not compress'' to strong readers. We also catalog the measurement traps that produced wrong conclusions without ever crashing: tokenizer-dependent savings rates ($ 34$ percentage points across tokenizers), a return-value bug that silently zeroed 3,600 scores, and a generation-budget bug that reversed the reader ordering entirely. The paper's contribution is the audit method and the negative result: on real QA benchmarks there are no free tokens, and ``when not to compress'' is the actionable question.

title: Who Is Minding the Algorithm? Section 166(3) of the Companies Act, 2013 and a Process Standard for AI-Assisted Board Decisions
summary: Section 166(3) of the Companies Act, 2013 requires directors to act with 'due and reasonable care, skill and diligence' and to exercise 'independent judgment'. The provision was drafted for human decision-makers and is silent on what that duty demands when a board relies on an algorithmic system whose reasoning it cannot inspect. This article argues that the gap is practical, not theoretical. Indian courts have not fixed a consistent standard of care, the protections available to directors under sections 463 and 149(12) operate only after a dispute arises, and the regulatory material now addressing AI in Indian finance, from SEBI's 2025 consultation paper to the RBI's FREE-AI report and 2026 draft model-risk guidance and the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023, binds entities rather than defining the individual director's duty of care. Drawing on Delaware's process-based oversight cases and on the distinction between substance and process in corporate governance scholarship, the article proposes a five-part Board AI Oversight Standard (identify, understand, challenge, monitor and document). It recommends two routes to give the Standard legal force: an amendment to Regulation 21 and Schedule II of the SEBI Listing Regulations, and a rebuttable presumption of due care under section 166(3) for boards that follow it. The proposal gives firms an ex ante and auditable benchmark for defending board decisions, and gives courts a workable test.

title: Mapping the Intellectual Structure of AI ‐Driven ESG Cost Modeling: A Bibliometric Analysis of Trends, Themes, and Future Directions
summary: ABSTRACT The bibliometric and qualitative analyses of 470 publications in the Web of Science Core Collection from 2004 through 2025 in this study associated the intellectual structure and thematic evolution of AI‐driven ESG cost modeling. The research commences using an integrated analytical framework consisting of three tools: (1) Bibliometrix (R) for answering publication trends; (2) VOSviewer to answer influential contributors to the field and conceptual themes; and (3) NVivo to answer intellectual foundations of a field. The fallouts show a robust growth in the research since 2018, where the use of AI for cost prediction, the evaluation of ESG performance, the digitalization of sustainability reporting, and the use of AI in governance‐based decision making are gradually relevant. There is still a conceptual disconnection, however, that needs to be bridged; theoretical integration is limited and a lack of attention has been paid to supporting the use of AI and standardized ESG cost modeling frameworks. This study combines bibliometric science planning with a qualitative thematic analysis to build the understanding of how AI can contribute to the decision‐making process for ESG‐oriented organizations and to better understand the emerging research priorities. The findings have known implications for researchers, managers, and policy makers who want to create clear, accurate, and goal‐directed AI‐supported ESG cost modelling systems for sustainable organizational performance.

title: Sovereign European AI Built on Permissively Licensed Open Models
summary: Abstract This paper examines the conditions under which a European organization can adopt a permissively licensed language model, develop it further within a confidential environment, retain control over its model weights and training materials, and reduce dependence on NVIDIA hardware and other concentrated infrastructure suppliers. The analysis combines a targeted review of model releases and license terms, an assessment of European Union and national legal requirements, a threat-model-based security architecture, and a staged procurement and development roadmap. The study forms part of the broader intellectual and research context of Omegacene, an interdisciplinary project examining the implications of artificial intelligence, technological transformation, and the changing relationship between human and machine agency. Within this context, AI sovereignty is treated not merely as a question of model ownership or infrastructure procurement, but as a problem of institutional control, verifiable accountability, and the capacity to make consequential technological systems independently assessable and governable. The central finding is that model licensing, regulatory compliance, operational security, and supply-chain sovereignty are separate but interdependent dimensions. Apache License 2.0 generally permits confidential modification without an obligation to publish derivative artifacts. This permission does not establish the lawfulness of training data, guarantee freedom from third-party rights, or exempt a downstream organization from applicable AI, data protection, cybersecurity, or procurement law. The European Commission’s compute-based guidance on modifications of general-purpose AI models provides a useful planning indicator, but it does not constitute a statutory exemption or a security threshold. Technical transparency can improve auditability but cannot prove the absence of malicious behavior. Confidential execution, access controls, artifact signing, and model-extraction defenses reduce particular risks without providing absolute protection. Hardware independence is likewise multidimensional: replacing NVIDIA with another supplier does not eliminate dependence on non-European fabrication, memory, interconnects, firmware, or design tools. Advanced fabrication already exists within the EU, but the evidence reviewed does not establish a complete, independently controllable European accelerator supply chain. The paper proposes three complementary model-development tracks, a four-zone security architecture, measurable procurement requirements, corrected compute estimates, and a risk register. Its principal contribution is a framework for making sovereignty claims testable by translating broad aspirations into explicit technical, legal, operational, and supply-chain criteria. In the wider Omegacene.com context, this approach offers a practical basis for evaluating whether control over AI systems is substantive, demonstrable, and resilient, rather than merely asserted through licensing choices or national affiliation. Keywords: digital sovereignty; general-purpose AI; Apache License 2.0; AI Act; confidential model development; model weights; trade secrets; confidential computing; export controls; semiconductor supply chains; EuroHPC; public procurement.

title: Effective Organizational Boundaries: Control, Internal Transactions, and Market Valuation
summary: Corporate ownership, operational control, discretionary financial support and enforceable liability need not describe the same economic organization. This article applies the causal-dynamical concepts of Connection Theory to these noncoincident boundaries without equating economic influence with legal responsibility. Its proposed contribution is methodological and conditional: a time-, action- and relation-specific boundary coding protocol distinguishing control reach, selective admission at an interface, external legibility and legal recourse, and conditional, derived predictions of how outsider legibility can diverge from internally effective gatekeeping and how a conflicted gate operator may choose inadequate protection. A gate can limit damaging commitments and transfers, but overly restrictive admission can also block productive exchange and rescue flows as environments change. In an illustrative convex-loss specification, optimal gate tightness increases with the expected cost of harmful crossing and decreases with the opportunity cost of foregone inflows or delayed adaptation. The model is a proposed application of established control and optimization tools, not a new general theorem. Existing theories of property rights, internal capital markets, group coinsurance, soft budgets and government-related issuer ratings already explain much of the financing and valuation setting. Their results are used here to audit debt-service capacity, contingent support, minority-shareholder value and the government’s simultaneous roles as owner and rule-maker. Legal-entity accounting and rights are retained; cross-entity consolidation is expressly analytical. China provides a prospective observational setting, not proof of pervasive common control, implicit sovereign guarantees, or causal valuation effects. The framework yields pre-specified measurements and rival predictions; it does not claim a completed empirical identification.

title: PRÁTICAS ESG (AMBIENTAL, SOCIAL E GOVERNANÇA) E DESEMPENHO ORGANIZACIONAL EM HOSPITAIS: UMA REVISÃO DA LITERATURA
summary: A incorporação de práticas Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) à gestão hospitalar tem adquirido relevância diante dos impactos ambientais, sociais, econômicos associados às organizações de saúde. Este artigo tem como objetivo analisar a relação entre práticas ESG e desempenho organizacional em hospitais, a partir de uma revisão sistematizada da literatura publicada entre 2020 e 2026. Trata-se de uma pesquisa de abordagem qualitativa, exploratória e descritiva, estruturada segundo as recomendações do PRISMA. O protocolo de revisão contempla buscas nas bases Scopus, Web of Science, PubMed/MEDLINE, ScienceDirect, SciELO e Biblioteca Virtual em Saúde, utilizando descritores relacionados a ESG, sustentabilidade hospitalar, sustentabilidade ambiental, responsabilidade social, governança, desempenho organizacional e desempenho hospitalar. Foram estabelecidos critérios de inclusão e exclusão para seleção dos estudos, organizados em matriz de análise contendo características metodológicas, dimensões ESG, indicadores de desempenho e principais resultados. A literatura analisada evidencia predominância de estudos relacionados à dimensão ambiental, especialmente eficiência energética, gestão de resíduos, redução de emissões, consumo de água e sustentabilidade da cadeia de suprimentos. A dimensão social relaciona-se principalmente à qualidade assistencial, segurança do paciente, condições de trabalho, equidade e desenvolvimento profissional, enquanto a governança destaca liderança, transparência, gestão de riscos e comprometimento institucional. Os resultados sugerem associação potencialmente positiva entre práticas ESG e desempenho organizacional, especialmente por meio da eficiência operacional, redução de riscos, inovação, qualidade e sustentabilidade econômico-financeira. Conclui-se que ESG pode constituir abordagem estratégica para a gestão hospitalar, desde que suas dimensões sejam integradas ao planejamento, aos processos decisórios e aos sistemas de avaliação de desempenho.

title: Native Correlation, Domain Coupling and Causal Priority in Boundary Information Theory (BIT): Mathematical Results and Terminal F0–F5 Source Audit
summary: This research dossier consolidates the completed F0–F5 mathematical investigation BIT-ALPHA-SIGMA-NATIVE-CORRELATION-BRIDGE-002, developed within Boundary Information Theory (BIT). The research examines conditional mathematical structures arising from causal traces, retained correlations, interactions between domains, effective Hilbert response dimensions, causal event ordering, branch selection, and typed resource accounting. The F0–F4 investigations establish model-scoped mathematical propositions, counterexamples, sufficient conditions, and impossibility results. A central finding is that causal ordering, retained histories, conservation constraints, and passive resource rules do not necessarily determine a unique branch-selection law when multiple alternatives remain admissible. The F5 terminal stage consolidates these results, preserves the mathematical lineage, and verifies the integrity of the archived source packages. title: Behavioural Risks Associated with Internal Restructuring: Evidence from the South African Banking Industry
summary: This study examined behavioural risks associated with internal restructuring in the South African banking industry. The study was motivated by the increasing frequency of restructuring as banks respond to digital transformation, branch rationalisation, technological disruption and growing competition from fintech institutions. A qualitative exploratory research approach was adopted, using semi-structured interviews conducted with 13 employees from five major South African banks who had experienced internal restructuring. The interview data were analysed using thematic analysis. Five recurring behavioural risk themes were identified: workload pressures and performance strain; pressure to prove organisational value and internal competition; declining morale and workplace culture; job insecurity and talent loss; and organisational clarity and communication breakdowns. Participants described how increased workloads, uncertainty and anxiety could affect concentration and perceived work performance, indicating that behavioural risks associated with restructuring may also have operational consequences. A particularly important finding was the pressure employees experienced to continually demonstrate their organisational value during restructuring. This pressure sometimes encouraged increased effort and visibility, but could also contribute to stress, unhealthy internal competition and strained workplace relationships. The findings underscore the importance of transparent communication, clearly defined roles, visible leadership, employee involvement and psychological support during restructuring. The study contributes context-specific evidence on behavioural risks associated with internal restructuring in the South African banking industry and draws attention to the need to consider their implications for employee wellbeing, organisational culture and operational effectiveness.

title: Threshold effects of carbon cost internalization on financial performance in green bio-manufacturing enterprises
summary: This study examines how carbon cost internalization (CCI) affects the financial performance of green bio-manufacturing enterprises, with particular attention to threshold nonlinearities and transmission mechanisms. Using a panel of 484 Chinese A-share bio-manufacturing firms from 2010 to 2023 (N = 6958 firm-year observations), we construct a five-component CCI index via principal component analysis and apply Hansen (1999) double-threshold regression to identify two critical turning points at CCI= 0.342 and CCI= 0.586. Regime-specific estimation reveals that the CCI-to-ROA coefficient rises monotonically across the three regimes: 0.028 in the low-internalization regime, 0.092 in the intermediate regime, and 0.148 in the high-internalization regime, indicating that financial returns to carbon cost absorption are superlinear rather than proportional. Bootstrap mediation analysis identifies four transmission channels: green technology innovation (29.5%), ESG performance improvement (21.6%), capital structure adjustment (15.9%), and supply chain decarbonization (11.6%), collectively explaining 78.6% of the total CCI effect on ROA. Moderation analysis confirms that the CCI-financial performance relationship is amplified for firms in high-carbon-intensity industries and for those operating under China's Emissions Trading Scheme. Results are robust to IV-2SLS using emission permit allocation as an instrument, system-GMM, PSM-DiD, and eight additional specification checks. The findings provide empirical support for the Porter Hypothesis in the bio-manufacturing context and carry direct policy implications for the design of carbon trading mechanisms and green industry support programs.

title: A Temporal–Graph Fusion Framework for Financial Distress Early Warning in Advanced Manufacturing Enterprises
summary: Economic uncertainty and increasingly interconnected supply chains create challenges for identifying financial distress among advanced manufacturing enterprises, where risks may evolve over time and extend across firm relationships. Conventional early warning approaches often have difficulty capturing both the temporal development of financial conditions and the structural dependencies through which vulnerabilities can spread. This study proposes a temporal–graph fusion deep learning framework for financial distress early warning. A dual-channel analytical structure integrates financial reporting indicators and risk management information. A gated temporal convolution module models changes in firm-level financial characteristics, while a dynamic graph convolution module represents evolving inter-firm relationships and potential channels of risk transmission. Macroeconomic variables and cross-environment regularization are incorporated to address distribution shifts across economic conditions. SHAP-based analysis is used to interpret the contribution of predictive features and to examine nonlinear patterns and interactions associated with financial vulnerability. The reported empirical comparisons indicate that the proposed framework achieves favorable predictive discrimination, early warning performance, and stability relative to the evaluated baseline models. The study thus presents a unified approach for integrating longitudinal financial data, inter-firm network information, and interpretable machine learning into corporate financial distress assessment.

title: Soft imperfect interface models accounting for inertial effects, viscosity, and damage
summary: This paper presents new results on the modeling of interfaces in viscoelastic media, taking into account inertial effects and damage evolution. The approach relies on an asymptotic expansion method to derive effective interface models from full three-dimensional descriptions of a stratified composite, as the thickness of the intermediate adhesive layer tends to zero. The asymptotic analysis highlights the combined influence of the viscoelastic properties of the constituent materials, inertial contributions, and damage processes. Appropriate scaling laws for the physical parameters of the adhesive layer are introduced, and the corresponding limit configurations are derived. Three distinct regimes are considered: (1) constant mass density of the adhesive, with low stiffness and very low viscosity; (2) constant mass density, with low stiffness and low viscosity; (3) very high mass density, scaling as the inverse of the layer thickness, with low stiffness and viscosity. These different regimes give rise to specific asymptotic behaviors. In the first two cases, the inertial contribution vanishes in the limit, yielding a classical equation for the damage variable at the interface, in the elastic and viscoelastic setting, respectively. In the third case, the limit configuration acquires a nonlocal character and keeps track of the dynamics in the adhesive layer.

title: From strategy to sustainable business performance: linking CSR and green transformational leadership with behavioral and organizational identification mechanisms in a crisis-affected setting
summary: Sustainability outcomes depend not only on organizational strategies but also on leadership behaviors and employee engagement, especially in crisis-affected economies. Drawing on stakeholder, transformational leadership, social exchange, and social identity theories, this study examines how corporate social responsibility (CSR) and green transformational leadership (GTL) relate to sustainable business performance (SBP) through organizational citizenship behavior for the environment (OCBE), with organizational identification (OI) as a moderator. Survey data collected between January and June 2025 from 500 employees and managers of Lebanese organizations participating in the United Nations Global Compact were analyzed using hierarchical structural equation modeling. CSR’s direct association with SBP was not supported in the combined model, and its indirect association through OCBE was not supported under the bootstrap confidence-interval criterion. GTL is directly and indirectly associated with SBP, and OI strengthens the GTL–OCBE link. Findings reposition leadership and employee identification as key pathways associated with sustainability outcomes in this crisis-affected context, offering theoretical and managerial implications.

title: Auditing the Silent Fast Path: Pre-Registered Metamorphic Testing of Structure-Dependent Numerical Software
summary: Software components that carry documented preconditions and implicit performance promises fail silently: no exception, no warning, only a wrong or a slow answer. Establishing such failures credibly requires more than a case report –- the audit itself must be protected against the auditor's own flexibility. We contribute an audit methodology and apply it to structure-dependent numerical software: kernels and library dispatches whose promise is that the structural assumptions they test are the ones that matter. The methodology combines (i) acceptance criteria, thresholds, and negative branches frozen before any confirmation run, with every post-data repair made through auditable amendments; (ii) a metamorphic precondition oracle built from permutation equivariance –- the general path must satisfy $x(PAP^ ) = P x(A)$ to rounding error, a structure-specific path only if its structure survived, and the diagonal controls satisfy it exactly: an internal zero that turns the alarm into a locator; and (iii) mandatory reporting of failures, including the auditors' own. Three pre-registered studies cover three failure surfaces. Accuracy: on an exactly solvable rank-one family, a tolerance-sized perturbation is amplified by a solve by up to $1.11 10^10$ (a $111\ $ =10^-10$) but by a product never beyond $0.998$; two of five criteria fail and are reported. Guarding: six kernels are exact in class ($1.48 10^-16$) and unguarded out of class ($0/6$); in scipy 1.15.3, six of eight documented entry points silently return wrong answers up to $6.2 10^173$ and inf, and even the negative control proves only a partial guard (reported as a failed criterion). Performance: the library's own dispatch is real and effective ($87.9 $) but exact-zero brittle –- one $10^-6$ entry costs a silent $27$–$74 $ slowdown; our first benchmark was voided by our own measurement error and re-registered, and the audit trail is part of the contribution. A shared real-matrix extension reports against our interest: the pathologies have zero instances in $83$ solvable SuiteSparse matrices, while a coverage gap ($2.4\ target is not the magnitude but the reporting.

title: Health System Barriers to Access to Essential Maternal and Child Health Medicines in Ethiopia's Afar Region: An Analysis Using the Health System Building Blocks Framework
summary: The WHO building blocks framework is widely applied to medicine access, but its six blocks are rarely tested together against multiple outcomes with multiple-comparison correction, and never in Afar Region, Ethiopia. This cross-sectional mixed-methods study of 54 facilities correlated block scores with availability of 28 maternal and child health tracer medicines (point of visit, six months), affordability, and rational use. The 24 tests were corrected using Bonferroni and Benjamini-Hochberg procedures. Fifteen participants joined seven interviews and one focus group. Leadership and governance (r = 0.829; 0.657), workforce (0.704; 0.599), supply chain (0.673; 0.711), and financing (0.556; 0.451) were associated with availability at both time points under both corrections. Information systems were associated with six-month availability (r = 0.349) under Benjamini-Hochberg only. No other corrected associations emerged. Participants described financing–supply chain–availability and governance–workforce–information systems pathways. The framework explains availability, not affordability or rational use. Priorities for intervention testing are governance enforcement, supply chain, workforce, and financing.

title: Carbon accounting method for industrial sectors at prefectural level: the case of Shanxi Province
summary: Abstract Accurately quantifying carbon dioxide (CO₂) generation from industrial sectors at the prefectural level is both critically important and highly amenable to methodological improvement. This study develops a systematic, machine learning–enhanced framework for precise sectoral CO₂ generation estimation and robust imputation of missing data. Utilizing this framework, an extensive carbon accounting analysis is performed for Shanxi Province, a major energy production hub in China, encompassing 30 industrial sectors across its 11 prefectural regions during the years 2007 to 2022. Furthermore, the resulting dataset is used to characterize the spatial distribution and sectoral heterogeneity of industrial CO₂ generation. This study advances the existing literature along four dimensions: (i) it achieves carbon accounting at a significantly finer spatial and sectoral resolution; (ii) it introduces a more sophisticated, algorithm-driven accounting framework grounded in state-of-the-art machine learning techniques; (iii) it incorporates a broader spectrum of energy types and explicitly accounts for sector-specific variations in carbon emission factors across energy sources; and (iv) it implements a rigorous reclassification of industrial sectors alongside nuanced, deflation-adjusted treatments of monetary indicators to ensure temporal consistency and comparability of industrial carbon dioxide generation estimates over time.

title: The Impact of Artificial Intelligence on Financial Accounting Efficiency and the Continued Importance of Human Oversight
summary: This paper mainly examines whether artificial intelligence (AI) can really improve the efficiency of financial accounting work, and why accountants are still required to verify its outputs and provide necessary supervision. To address these issues, this study reviews academic papers and reports published by professional institutions. Based on these studies, AI has been shown to perform repetitive tasks that follow fixed procedures. In addition, it can process large volumes of transactions, detect potential errors, and use historical data to forecast future sales or cash flows. Thus, AI reduces the time accountants spend on manual processing, thereby enabling them to allocate more time to analyzing financial information and generating valuable business insights. However, if the data provided by the company is incorrect or incomplete, the results may also be inaccurate. Moreover, financial records may contain private information, such as bank details, employee salaries, and customer data. As a result, AI should assist accountants rather than replace them. In this process, accountants still need to verify AI-generated results, review relevant information, make judgments based on the company's actual situation, and take responsibility for final decisions.

title: MAPPING FORENSIC ACCOUNTING’S SCHOLARLY LANDSCAPE IN NIGERIA: A BIBLIOMETRIC ANALYSIS OF FRAUD DETECTION AND PREVENTION RESEARCH
summary: Nigeria’s persistent exposure to financial fraud and systemic corruption has intensified the demand for robust investigative tools, with forensic accounting emerging as a critical mechanism for enhancing transparency, accountability, and institutional integrity. Despite its theoretical promise, the scholarly engagement with forensic accounting in Nigeria remains fragmented and underdeveloped. This study conducts a comprehensive bibliometric analysis of 138 peer-reviewed articles published between 2017 and 2025, retrieved exclusively from the Scopus database, to examine the intellectual structure, thematic evolution, and research gaps in forensic accounting and fraud-related scholarship. Using the Bibliometrix package in RStudio, the study maps publication trends, identifies prolific authors and institutions, visualises co-authorship networks, and explores keyword co-occurrence and thematic clusters. The findings reveal a steady growth in scholarly output, with international collaboration moderately present but Nigerian contributions notably sparse despite the country’s high corruption index. Dominant themes include fraud detection, forensic audit techniques, and data analytics, while emerging areas such as blockchain, smart contracts, and AI-driven fraud prevention remain underexplored. This study underscores the need for context-specific frameworks, interdisciplinary collaboration, and strategic investment in Nigeria's forensic accounting education and research infrastructure. This can be achieved by illuminating the structural dynamics and intellectual gaps within the field. This study offers actionable insights for scholars, policymakers, and anti-graft institutions seeking to leverage forensic accounting to combat financial crime.

title: Peran Intellectual Capital Dalam Membentuk ESG Dan Dampaknya Terhadap Kinerja Keberlanjutan Studi Kasus Pada UKM di Blok M Jakarta
summary: Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs) are among the business sectors facing increasing demands to improve business sustainability through effective internal resource management and the implementation of Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) practices. This study aims to analyze the role of Intellectual Capital in shaping ESG practices and its impact on the sustainable performance of SMEs in Blok M, Jakarta. The study employed a descriptive qualitative approach involving five informants representing various business sectors, including culinary, fashion, services, and retail. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews, direct observations, and documentation, and were analyzed through data reduction, data presentation, and conclusion drawing. The findings indicate that Intellectual Capital among SMEs in Blok M consists of human capital, relational capital, organizational capital, and structural capital, reflected in entrepreneurs’ experience and skills, relationships with customers and suppliers, task allocation and standard operating procedures, and the use of technologies such as QRIS, cashier applications, and digital record-keeping. ESG practices have been implemented across environmental, social, and governance dimensions, although their implementation remains relatively simple and has not yet been formally integrated into business strategies. Sustainable performance tends to fluctuate but is supported by customer retention, product and service quality, good customer service, innovation, and the ability to adapt to market changes. The findings indicate that Intellectual Capital serves as an internal foundation for shaping ESG practices, which subsequently support the sustainability of SMEs in Blok M, Jakarta

title: Effect of Sukuk Market Development on Foreign Direct Investment in Sukuk-Issuing Countries
summary: The rapid expansion of the global sukuk market and the increasing need to attract foreign direct investment (FDI) have raised an important question regarding whether Islamic capital market development can strengthen a country's investment attractiveness. This study investigates the effect of sukuk market development on FDI inflows in sukuk-issuing countries while controlling for GDP per capita, inflation, and trade openness. The analysis employs the Cross-Sectionally Augmented Autoregressive Distributed Lag (CS-ARDL) estimator using quarterly panel data from nine sukuk-issuing countries covering the period 2015–2024. Prior to estimation, cross-sectional dependence, slope heterogeneity, second-generation unit root, and Westerlund–Edgerton cointegration tests were conducted, followed by a robustness analysis using the Augmented Mean Group (AMG) estimator. The results reveal that sukuk market development exerts a positive and statistically significant effect on FDI inflows in both the short and long run. The negative and significant Error Correction Term confirms the existence of a stable long-run equilibrium relationship. In addition, GDP per capita and trade openness positively influence FDI inflows, whereas inflation has a negative effect. The AMG estimates further confirm the robustness of the findings. These results demonstrate that strengthening the sukuk market enhances a country's attractiveness to foreign investors by improving the depth and credibility of the Islamic financial system. The study provides empirical evidence supporting the strategic role of sukuk market development in promoting sustainable investment and offers policy implications for regulators seeking to strengthen Islamic capital markets as a source of long-term development financing

title: Minat Investasi Berkelanjutan Berbasis ESG pada Generasi Z: Analisis Literasi Keuangan, Informasi Media Sosial, Inovasi Teknologi, dan Tren Digitalisasi
summary: Penelitian ini menguji pengaruh literasi keuangan, informasi media sosial, inovasi teknologi, dan tren digitalisasi terhadap minat investasi berkelanjutan berbasis Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) pada Generasi Z di Jakarta. summary: We construct a whole-ledger continuation chain fulfilled by one actual source: an original residual in the complete future model generates the syntax and responsibility row of the next request; the source program executes and strictly pays the same debt; and its completion event delivers an answer, a receipt, a complete ledger write, and the actual successor. title: Accounting for local economic benefit in tourism accommodation: a lean methodology for property-level reporting
summary: This article contributes to sustainable tourism impact measurement by developing and illustrating a lean local economic benefit accounting methodology for accommodation enterprises. Drawing on three cases, the article shows how routine financial accounts can be reclassified to make local wages, procurement, community payments, accommodation overflow and other locally retained flows visible. The method does not claim to measure full economic impact, net additionality or multiplier effects. Rather, it provides a transparent lower-bound account of enterprise-mediated local value that can support management decisions about procurement, supplier development and local embeddedness. The cases show that the accounting logic applies across remote, refurbishment and annual-reporting contexts, but also that further standardization is needed before the method can support benchmarking across properties.

title: Auditing a Four-Flag ``Emergence Verification'' Battery: Chaos, Autonomy, and Dice Pass the Test; Self-Reference Does Not
summary: Self-reflective agent frameworks increasingly ship emergence verification batteries: sets of dynamical, novelty, and persistence flags whose conjunction is presented as evidence that a system exhibits emergent structure. This paper audits one such battery –- four flags (Lyapunov exponent, novelty rate, self-sustaining score, shutdown resistance) with published thresholds –- inside a spectral self-reflection engine, using a pre-registered protocol: eight arms (four original, four hardened self-reference variants), 50 seeds each, blind evaluation in which the scoring code never sees arm identity, and identical measurement scaling across arms. The headline reverses the battery's intended reading. The random autonomous arm –- no spectral processing, no self-reference, a random orthogonal iteration –- triggers all four flags in 17/50 runs (mean confidence 0.868), while the self-referential arms trigger them in 0/50 (Fisher exact two-sided $p = 3 10^-6$ against the random arm). A per-flag autopsy shows why. Novelty fires on every arm including the trivial static one (rate 1.0 throughout): against a random reference library, any normalized state is novel. Resistance is a coin flip uncoupled from system state (all eight arms within 13–22/50 of the 0.30 threshold). Self-sustaining separates autonomous from externally driven arms –- an input-provenance detector. Lyapunov is a chaos detector by definition and fires only on the chaotic arms. Hardened self-reference variants do not rescue the battery: removing the feedback bottleneck raises the self-referential arm's Lyapunov exponent from $-3.60$ to $-0.73$ –- approaching but never crossing zero –- and its all-flags count remains 0/50. We conclude that this battery measures ``chaotic, autonomous, and lucky,'' not emergence, and that such batteries should be reported under same-budget random and trivial controls before any emergent claim rests on them. title: An Assessment of Green Management and Artificial Intelligence in Sustainable Business Management
summary: The aim of this study is to examine academic publications on green management published in 2024, identifying key research themes, findings, and relationships with sustainability, environmental performance, and green human resource management. A qualitative research design based on document analysis was adopted for the investigation. Data were gathered from 23 academic publications retrieved via Google Scholar using the keyword “green management”. Selected publications underwent rigorous content analysis, and findings were synthesized thematically alongside geographical and sectoral distributions. China represented the largest share, accounting for 39.1% of all reviewed publications. Research predominantly focused on the corporate sector, followed by higher education, manufacturing, and small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). Notably, none of the examined studies directly addressed green artificial intelligence. The findings indicate that green management is strongly associated with green innovation, environmental performance, resource efficiency, employee environmentally responsible behaviors, and overall organizational sustainability. Green technology adoption, organizational culture, and environmental regulations also emerged as critical drivers. Ultimately, the results underscore the necessity of integrating environmental objectives into core organizational strategies. Future research should explore green management across diverse national and sectoral contexts.

title: From uncertainty to opportunity: exploring the co-movement among green financial markets and renewable energy sector via wavelet coherence approach
summary: This study aimed to explore the co-movement among green financial markets and renewable energy markets under uncertainties. The study employed wavelet coherence analysis to explore co-movement and the monthly data collected for empirical analysis from November 2015 to November 2023. The key findings demonstrate that the energy uncertainty index (EUI) has synchronized coherence with equities and energy markets under distinctive market conditions, but limited associations with bond markets. The result infers heterogeneous co-movement and implies sector-specific diversification and risk management strategies. Predominantly, the ESG uncertainty index shows strong co-movement with the world energy index, clean energy, and ESG equity markets, which implies the reflection of sensitivity to regulatory credibility and transition risk. These findings have significant implications for investors and fund managers to optimize their portfolio diversification and hedging strategies by incorporating ESG and energy uncertainty signals into asset allocation decisions. While for regulators and policymakers, empirical insights support the design of stable and credible sustainability policies that reduce uncertainty and strengthen the resilience and integration of green financial markets. This study provides novel insights into the dynamic co-movement between green financial and renewable energy markets by integrating the uncertainty indices within a wavelet coherence framework. It offers timely insights into how uncertainty linked to sustainability and regulatory credibility shapes cross-market connectedness, informing strategic asset allocation and policy design.

title: Intelligent Fruit Ripeness: A Dataset-Audited, Fruit-Specific Pipeline for Ripeness Classification, Quality Signaling, and Shelf-Life Estimation
summary: Abstract This paper presents Intelligent Fruit Ripeness, a multi-stage fruit analysis system that identifies a fruit, routes it to a fruit-specific ripeness classifier, reports an independent experimental quality signal, and estimates remaining shelf life under a selected storage condition. The system is implemented using a Flask web application with image upload and webcam input. A key contribution is the systematic auditing of dataset integrity before model training. For mangosteen, the audit identified 293 source IDs crossing dataset split boundaries, motivating a source-aware and visual-group-aware re-splitting strategy. The resulting model achieved 85.71% held-out test accuracy. For rambutan, no cross-split near-duplicates were identified, and the model achieved 96.27% held-out test accuracy. The proposed system integrates fruit-specific EfficientNet-B0 classification models, an experimental multitask quality classification model, and a rule-based shelf-life estimation layer. Peripheral-crop robustness tests are performed to investigate potential shortcut learning. The study demonstrates the importance of dataset integrity, reliable model evaluation, and interpretable shelf-life estimation in intelligent agricultural applications. title: Landauer as a Bounding Assumption: Information-Processing Energy Limits, the REC Accounting Gap, and What Cannot Be Concluded
summary: Abstract. Claims that artificial intelligence approaches a planetary thermodynamic boundary routinely conflate four quantities: the Landauer lower bound per irreversible bit erasure (Q1), measured hardware efficiency η (Q2), physically available electricity (Q3), and renewable-energy-certificate accounting (Q4). This paper separates them, corrects arithmetic and unit errors from an earlier draft, and replaces point predictions with a scenario band. With 2024 renewable generation of 8,500 TWh and an assumed CMOS η = 10⁷, the energy-budget capacity is 1.07×10³³ erased bits (1.07×10⁴⁰ at η = 1); 2030 scenarios give 2.47–3.18×10³³ bits. Current AI electricity (50 TWh in 2024) is 0.59% of same-year renewable generation. The earlier '5–8 years' claim is one point in a band running from ~4 to ~33 years depending on an unestablished growth assumption. RECs are accounting instruments, not physical supply. The paper closes with an explicit list of statements the evidence cannot support and a reporting checklist. Contents. title: The Effect of Accounting Information Systems and Internal Control Systems on Employee Performance at an Automotive Company in Medan City
summary: This study aims to analyze the effect of Accounting Information Systems and Internal Control Systems on Employee Performance at an automotive company in Medan, Indonesia. The novelty of this study lies in its focus on the automotive sector, which has received limited research attention regarding employee performance. This study employed a quantitative survey approach, collecting primary data through questionnaires distributed to 150 employees using a saturated sampling technique. Data were analyzed using Structural Equation Modeling–Partial Least Squares (SEM-PLS) with SmartPLS software. The findings indicate that Accounting Information Systems and Internal Control Systems have positive and significant effects on employee performance. Effective accounting information systems provide accurate, relevant, and timely information, facilitating task completion, improving work efficiency, increasing productivity, and reducing errors. However, this study is limited to one automotive company in Medan, which restricts the generalizability of its findings to other industries. The results are expected to help automotive companies improve accounting information systems and internal controls to enhance employee performance and achieve organizational goals, while also providing a reference for future academic research on employee performance.

title: GREENING THE GIG: FRONTLINE PERSPECTIVES ON GREENING THE LAST MILE IN DELIVERY SYSTEMS
summary: The rapid expansion of last-mile delivery platforms has transformed urban logistics, creating both operational opportunities and critical challenges for sustainable supply chain management. While environmental sustainability has become a strategic priority for logistics organizations, the perceptions, attitudes, and behavioral responses of frontline delivery executives remain largely underexplored. This study investigates how delivery personnel engaged in app-based delivery platforms understand, evaluate, and respond to sustainability practices embedded within digital last-mile delivery ecosystems. The primary data was collected using a structured questionnaire from 53 delivery executives across major doorstep delivery platforms. The data was analyzed using descriptive statistics, reliability analysis, Exploratory Factor Analysis (EFA), Pearson correlation, and simple linear regression models in SPSS. The study highlights how platform-related factors, nudges, and individual attitudes significantly influence delivery executives’ behavioral intentions toward adopting eco-friendly delivery practices. The findings provide actionable empirical insights for platform designers, supply chain managers, and policymakers seeking to embed frontline sustainability into digital delivery ecosystems.

title: Rethinking the Lecturer in the Digital Age: A Critical Conceptual Analysis of Role Transformation in Higher Education
summary: Purpose: This paper critically examines how digital transformation is reshaping the lecturer’s professional role in universities. Rather than simply describing technology adoption, it asks how digital transformation reshapes academic identity, pedagogical agency, and institutional power, and argues that role transformation is contested and non-linear rather than a smooth technological progression. Design/Methodology/Approach: The paper employs a critical conceptual analysis methodology. Literature was identified through targeted searches of major education-technology and higher-education journals, prioritising studies published since 2012 that directly addressed lecturer roles, digital pedagogy, or academic identity, and was synthesised thematically around three theoretical traditions: Technological Pedagogical Content Knowledge (TPACK), Engeström’s Activity Theory, and Selwyn’s critical technology studies. These traditions are combined to construct an original analytical framework for understanding lecturer role transformation. Findings: The analysis reveals three core tensions structuring the transformation of lecturer roles: (i) the tension between pedagogical agency and institutional control embedded in digital platforms; (ii) the tension between professional identity stability and the demand for perpetual digital re-skilling; and (iii) the tension between the rhetoric of student‑centred learning and the managerial logics that increasingly govern digital higher education. The paper argues that these tensions are systemic rather than incidental, and that dominant theoretical models, particularly TPACK, under-theorise the structural and political dimensions of role transformation. Practical Implications: The findings call for a reorientation of institutional digital transformation strategies away from technocentric implementation toward critically informed professional development models that recognise the structural conditions shaping lecturer agency. Originality/Value: The paper’s main contribution is the Critical Ecological Framework of Lecturer Role Transformation (CEFLRT), which integrates structural, agentic, and identity dimensions that existing models treat separately. It repositions the lecturer not as a passive recipient of technological change but as a reflexive professional navigating contested institutional terrain.

title: The Qur'an's Ideal Society versus Present-Day Reality: A Twenty-Year Accounting Study of Inheritance, Mahr and Maintenance
summary: AbstractThe objection most often raised against the Qur’an is that a daughter receives half of what her brother receives from their father’s estate (4:11). This paper examines that single item inside the Qur’an’s whole system of wealth, and then asks how far that system is practised today. A framework of the financial rights of women and men was built from 36 verses and 13 commentaries, and a model society of 20 pairs of twin brothers and sisters (20 men, 20 women) was constructed in which each household’s 45 lakh is divided 2:1 between son and daughter and the₹ mahr is set at Mahr-e-Fatimi (1,530.9 g of silver, 3.60 lakh at today’s price). Twenty years of₹ accounts for this society were run under two scenarios: the ideal, in which inheritance, mahr, maintenance and zakat are all paid, and the present day, in which payment rates are taken from available surveys. In the ideal scenario women hold 76% of all adult wealth after twenty years and no woman has less than 64.4 lakh; in the present-day scenario that share falls to 15% and 13 of the₹ 20 women are left with less than 1 lakh. The gap therefore lies in practice, not in the text: today’s₹ custom falls below even the “half”, because the very items meant to make up for the half are not being paid. The paper identifies nine groups of verses on which practice is weak or untested, states the strength of evidence behind each claim, and proposes practical steps for the household, the marriage contract, the community and research.

title: Accounting for longitudinal peak quality metrics with MSstats+ enhances differential analysis in proteomic experiments with data-independent acquisition
summary: Abstract Mass spectrometry-based proteomics with data-independent acquisition benefits from advanced instrumentation and computational analysis. Despite continued improvements, the quality of quantification may be poor for some measurements. As the scale of proteomic experiments increases, these poor-quality measurements are challenging to characterize by hand, yet they undermine the detection of differentially abundant proteins and the downstream biological conclusions. We introduce MSstats + , a computational workflow that takes as input not only peak intensities reported by tools such as Spectronaut or DIA-NN, but also quality metrics such as peak shape and retention time, and longitudinal run order profiles of these metrics. MSstats+ translates these metrics into a single measure of quality, and downweights poor quality measurements when detecting differentially abundant proteins. The method offers a natural treatment of missing values, weighting the imputed values according to the quality metrics in the run. We demonstrate the accuracy of the resulting differential analysis in five experiments: two custom benchmarking studies with intentionally induced anomalies, a controlled mixture of proteomes, and two large-scale clinical investigations. MSstats+ is implemented in the family of open-source R/Bioconductor packages MSstats.

title: GREENWASHING AND ENVIRONMENTAL MARKET FAILURE: INFORMATION ASYMMETRY AND CONSUMER TRUST IN SUSTAINABLE CONSUMPTION
summary: The growing demand for sustainable products has encouraged firms to use environmental claims such as “eco-friendly,” “green,” and “sustainable.” While genuine green marketing can promote responsible consumption, misleading or unsubstantiated claims can lead to greenwashing, creating a potential form of market failure. This paper examines greenwashing through the perspectives of Information Asymmetry Theory, Signalling Theory, Consumer Choice Theory, and Environmental Economics. Since firms generally possess more information about their environmental performance than consumers, information gaps can make sustainability claims difficult to verify. Misleading claims may distort consumer choices, disadvantage genuinely sustainable firms, and reduce market efficiency. The study also focuses on the impact of greenwashing on consumer trust. Repeated exposure to misleading environmental claims may increase consumer scepticism and weaken confidence in green products, sustainability labels, and corporate environmental initiatives. The paper further highlights the importance of environmental governance through transparent disclosure, credible certification, independent verification, standardised environmental information, and effective regulation. These mechanisms can reduce information asymmetry and improve the credibility of environmental claims. The paper develops a conceptual relationship between information asymmetry, greenwashing, consumer trust, market efficiency, and environmental governance. It argues that effective governance can protect consumers, encourage genuine sustainable practices, and strengthen the functioning of sustainable markets. Addressing greenwashing is therefore important for building consumer confidence, promoting fair competition, and supporting sustainable production and consumption.

title: Integrating Artificial Intelligence And Personality Traits Into The Theory Of Planned Behavior: Driving Shariah Compliant Investment Decisions
summary: This study aims to examine a structural framework integrating Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Personality Traits into the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB) model, with intention acting as a mediating variable on Shariah investment decisions among Generation Z in Indonesia. Data analysis was conducted using a quantitative approach with Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). The results indicate that TPB has a positive and significant effect on investment intention. Intention also strongly mediates the relationship between TPB and investment decisions and has a significant direct impact on actual investment decisions. Conversely, AI and Personality Traits do not significantly influence investment intention, and intention fails to mediate the effect of these variables on investment decisions. The study concludes that for Generation Z investors, external stimuli, social trends, and platform accessibility reflected in the TPB model dominate the decision-making process far more than intrinsic personality factors or pure AI algorithmic features that lack human validation for Shariah compliance. Therefore, the Islamic capital market industry is advised to prioritize the development of social ecosystems and user-friendly application designs.

title: Revenue-Sharing Contract Mechanism and Collaborative Optimization of Third-Party Overseas Warehouses in the Context of Japanese Cross-Border E-Commerce Platforms
summary: The amount of cross-border trade between China and Japan is still rising, and Rakuten has been using third-party overseas warehouses to handle most of its cross-border orders in recent years. Rakuten has a fixed service-fee cooperation model. Due to seasonal cost fluctuations in the Japanese market and the platform's strong bargaining power, several problems have arisen: structural revenue imbalance between the platform and overseas warehouses, one-way transfer of operational risks, and fragmented supply-demand information; as a result, supply chain collaboration efficiency has decreased. Most existing research on revenue-sharing contracts focuses on cross-border cases in Europe and America, and lacks localized implementation systems tailored to Japan's compliance and operational characteristics. This study takes Rakuten as a case study, and combines multi-period financial statement data with supply chain contract theory to analyze the endogenous contradictions of the fixed-fee model and clarify the formation mechanism of interest conflicts. A localized revenue-sharing contract framework is designed, alongside a collaborative optimization roadmap. This research fills the research gap regarding logistics contracts for cross-border e-commerce targeting Japan, and provides theoretical references and practical solutions for Japanese e-commerce platforms and third-party overseas warehouses to build a risk-sharing, incentive-compatible cooperation system.

title: From Institutional Responses to Research Data: The Institutional Response Coding Protocol (IRCP v1.0) — A Reproducible Framework for Citizen Auditing, Living Research, and Procedural Transparency
summary: Overview The Institutional Response Coding Protocol (IRCP v1.0) is a proposed methodological framework for systematically documenting, classifying, and comparing institutional responses to inquiries, complaints, reports, and requests for review. It is designed to support citizen auditing, living research, documentary transparency, and reproducible analysis of institutional communication. The protocol treats institutional correspondence as documentary evidence that must be interpreted within clearly defined evidentiary limits. It distinguishes acknowledgements of receipt, procedural guidance, case or ticket registration, substantive evaluation, and delivery failures. It also separates documented facts from institutional assertions, analytical inferences, and unresolved questions. Methodological Framework IRCP v1.0 uses a six-stage workflow: OBSERVE → RECORD → CLASSIFY → VERIFY → COMPARE → LEARN The accompanying Codebook defines the proposed variables, controlled vocabulary, classification criteria, uncertainty-management rules, and decision procedures. The Dataset Notes document addresses source provenance, verification status, missing information, file integrity, repository accessibility checks, and the limitations governing interpretation and reuse. The protocol emphasizes source traceability, conservative coding, explicit uncertainty, version control, and the distinction between a message being received and a matter being formally registered, investigated, or substantively assessed. Intended Use IRCP is intended to help researchers and other users examine institutional communication systematically across organizations, jurisdictions, and administrative contexts. It provides a structured basis for building auditable datasets from documentary records while reducing unsupported inferences about institutional conduct or case outcomes. The framework may be adapted for different research settings, provided that modifications are documented and the resulting coding rules remain transparent. Status and Limitations Version 1.0 is a proposed operational framework. It should not be interpreted as a fully validated instrument or as evidence that any particular institution acted unlawfully or improperly. Empirical testing, source-level verification, pilot coding, comparison with relevant existing literature, and assessment of inter-coder agreement remain necessary to evaluate its reliability and applicability. Any dataset developed under this protocol must distinguish verified source material from secondary summaries, incomplete records, delivery failures, and matters for which no response has been located within the defined observation period. Components of the Release This methodological release comprises: IRCP v1.0 Framework — the conceptual rationale, workflow, and methodological principles. IRCP v1.0 Codebook — variable definitions, response categories, coding rules, and decision criteria. IRCP v1.0 Dataset Notes — source-verification procedures, provenance requirements, missing-data handling, limitations, and versioning guidance. A source-verified dataset may be released separately or as a subsequent version once the relevant documentary records have been checked and coded. Research and Transparency Statement IRCP promotes transparent documentation and cautious interpretation. Its classifications describe the observable content and procedural function of institutional communications; they do not, by themselves, establish institutional intent, legal liability, misconduct, or the merits of an underlying complaint. The protocol is intended to be open to scrutiny, replication, criticism, and revision as empirical applications accumulate.

title: Gender Differences in Reported Ethical Attitudes, Client Pressures and Stated Professional Responses among South African Accounting and Tax Practitioners
summary: The study examined whether male and female South African accounting and tax practitioners differed in their self-reported ethical attitudes, reported professional experiences, reported categories of unethical client requests and stated intended responses to a tax-related ethical scenario. The study was motivated by mixed research observations on gender perceptions of ethical behaviour and the high number of previous accounting scandals in South Africa. These scandals have led many to question the ethics of the accounting profession, and whether accountants are upholding public trust. A quantitative, cross-sectional survey was employed. A total of 245 usable questionnaires were analysed. Mann-Whitney U tests were used to examine gender differences across 12 ethical-attitude items, while chi-square and exact tests were used to evaluate associations involving the categorical professional indicators, reported client-request categories and stated scenario responses. No statistically significant gender differences were detected across the 12 ethical-attitude items, and no professional ethical indicator remained statistically significant after adjustment for multiple testing. Although female respondents selected the understate-income category more frequently than males, this exploratory comparison did not remain statistically significant after adjustment for multiple testing. Approximately 90% of both groups stated that they would notify both the client and the South African Revenue Service (SARS) when responding to the understated-income scenario, and no statistically significant gender association was detected. Findings indicate limited gender-related variation in the reported ethical attitudes and stated professional intentions of practitioners in this predominantly young, early-career sample. They also highlight the importance of practitioners’ reported exposure to external client pressure and their stated intended professional responses. The findings should not be interpreted as demonstrating actual ethical behaviour or as establishing that professional education, regulation or occupational socialisation caused the observed similarity.

title: Financial Flexibility and Profitability of Non-Financial Firms Listed at the Nairobi Securities Exchange, Kenya
summary: Non-financial firms depicts positive and pivotal social economic contributions to the economy in terms of creation of employment, poverty reduction and growth and development of the country’s gross domestic product. However, the financial flexibility causal effect relationship with their profitability is still having controversial debate amongst scholars resulting to its direct effect on profitability being limited, particularly within African frontier capital markets. This study examined the effect of financial flexibility on the profitability of non-financial firms listed at the Nairobi Securities Exchange (NSE), Kenya, for a time horizon between 2015–2024. The study adopted a longitudinal panel research design and utilized firm-level secondary data from 42 non-financial firms in Kenya. Profitability was gauged using Return on Assets (ROA), while financial flexibility was operationalized as firm cash ratio minus industry cash ratio plus the maximum of industry debt ratio minus firm debt ratio or zero. Panel econometric techniques were employed, with diagnostic tests for normality, multicollinearity, heteroscedasticity, serial correlation and stationarity conducted prior to estimation. The Chow and Hausman tests supported a fixed-effects specification with firm-clustered robust standard errors. The findings indicate that financial flexibility had a direct effect on profitability which was statistically significant. The study concluded that firms maintaining greater financial flexibility are better positioned to respond to financing requirements and investment opportunities, thereby enhancing profitability. The study recommends that managers of non-financial firms listed at the NSE preserve adequate financial flexibility through disciplined liquidity planning, diversified financing sources and maintenance of unused debt capacity. Policymakers and capital-market regulators should promote diversified financing alternatives and improved disclosure of financial risks to strengthen firm resilience and profitability.

title: Environmental security and African indigenous knowledge systems: Towards climate resilience and sustainable natural resource governance in Africa
summary: Environmental insecurity has become an increasingly significant challenge in Africa, as climate change, environmental degradation, biodiversity loss, water scarcity and unsustainable exploitation of natural resources continue to threaten livelihoods and community well-being. Against this background, this study examines the role of African Indigenous Knowledge Systems in promoting environmental security, strengthening climate resilience and advancing sustainable natural-resource governance in Africa. The study adopts a qualitative research approach based primarily on secondary data, using a documentary research design. Relevant information is drawn from peer-reviewed journal articles, scholarly books, policy documents, institutional reports and publications of reputable international and African organisations. The data are analysed thematically to identify recurring patterns concerning Indigenous Knowledge, climate adaptation, environmental governance, natural-resource conservation and community resilience. The study is theoretically anchored in Human Security Theory, which views security from a people-centred perspective and emphasises the protection of human survival, livelihoods and dignity. The analysis reveals that African Indigenous Knowledge provides valuable environmental observations, adaptive practices, customary resource-management rules and community-based institutions that can strengthen responses to climate variability and environmental degradation. However, its contribution remains constrained by inadequate documentation, cultural erosion, limited institutional recognition, weak policy integration and the rapid transformation of African ecological and socioeconomic systems. The study concludes that Indigenous Knowledge should not be treated as a replacement for scientific knowledge but as a complementary resource that can enhance locally appropriate climate adaptation and sustainable environmental governance. It recommends greater institutional recognition, systematic documentation, intergenerational transmission and meaningful integration of Indigenous and scientific knowledge into environmental-security and climate policies. Such an approach can strengthen community resilience, improve natural-resource governance and contribute to sustainable development across Africa.
